items.title: Cardano Prototype Explores Trustless Swaps With Shielded Zcash
items.description: Cardano developer open-sources zeUTXO, a simulator-only prototype for trustless ADA-to-shielded Zcash atomic swaps without bridges, oracles, relays or light clients. The unaudited project seeks community review and development while highlighting the gap between cryptographic design and live network testing.

items.title: Digest November 11: UniHack 2026 | Linear Leios and Ouroboros Peras | Cardano's 2027 Events Proposal | New CIP Updates | Petrobras on Cardano | DijkstraNet Upgrade, and more
items.description: Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: UniHack 2026 & Developer Survey: Registrations are open for Sri Lanka’s UniHack, while the Cardano Developer Ecosystem Survey remains open until November 30. Leios & SPO Updates: The latest SPO discussions look ahead to Node 11.3 and the gradual rollout of Linear Leios. Ouroboros Peras: TWEAG has completed nine of twelve mainnet roadmap milestones, with a recent demo showcasing progress. Cardano Treasury Proposal: The Cardano Foundation submitted its 2027 Global Events proposal, requesting USD 4.99 million for activities across twelve cities. CIP Updates: New proposals cover Dynamic Rewards, governance role declarations and a Dijkstra-era Web-Wallet Bridge, while three others move into active review. Cardano Foundation Updates: From Petrobras tokenizing sustainable aviation fuel certificates to new case studies, UCLA collaboration, zero-knowledge research and the latest Accelerator cohort. Intersect & Governance Updates: Updates cover the proposed 2027 budget process, Dijkstra readiness, constitutional amendments, DRep activity and the upcoming Annual Members Meeting. All this and more in today’s Digest. CTA: UniHack 2026: Registrations Are Open For Sri Lanka’s Student Builders Calling the next generation of builders in Sri Lanka. CoinCeylon’s UniHack 2026 brings students from 20+ universities together to learn and build on Cardano and Midnight, with this year’s theme set as Blockchain for Real-World Adoption. Registrations close on 17 November, the building phase and workshops run to 15 December, and the finale lands on 17 December. There is a LKR 500,000 prize pool split LKR 250,000, LKR 150,000 and LKR 100,000 across the top three, five challenge categories from digital finance and real-world assets to privacy and governance, and judging weighted towards viability and adoption rather than polish. Submissions must be open source under Apache 2.0 with a two-to-four-minute demo. It is organised with the University of Kelaniya Faculty of Computing and Technology, the Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, and CSSA. Register here . Oh, and while we’re on the topic of developers, here are two other things worth a few minutes of your time. The developer survey. The 2026 State of the Cardano Developer Ecosystem survey stays open until 30 November: 15 minutes, nine languages, and this year the responses are recorded on-chain and linked to an Info Action. If you build on Cardano, it is the cheapest way to influence the next round of engineering priorities. Take it at devsurvey.cardano.org . ** The 2027 budget process.** Intersect and ecosystem partners want feedback on the proposed Cardano Ecosystem Budget Process before a first info action, targeted for 10 November, with a second round in December or January. Read the proposal and comment on DRepTalk or the Cardano Forum thread . Latest Updates on Ouroboros Peras + Product Demo From TWEAG Peras does not shout, it ships. And the latest update from the TWEAG team shows that things are moving along nicely. The Ouroboros Peras work, focused on speeding up settlement on Cardano, has now reached nine of the twelve milestones on its mainnet roadmap , according to the team’s tracker. So far, 76 pull requests have been merged, with a handful more still under review. On 2 November, the team shared a demo covering two months of progress across protocol design, consensus and testing. Definitely worth a look if you want to see what’s taking shape: the recording and slides are available here , alongside the video shared on X the following day. The weekly report from 6 November also offers a closer look at some of the technical work. One area the team is addressing is how to persist volatile certificates to disk, ensuring that certificates are never lost, while also working through how the volatile and immutable certificate sets overlap. Previous updates have covered voting rules, certificate sharing between nodes and local test network setup. If you enjoy following protocol development as it happens, CIP-0140 and the Peras tracker are two good places to keep an eye on. Cardano Global Events 2027 Treasury Proposal, by Cardano Foundation The Cardano Foundation has submitted a Treasury proposal for its 2027 global events programme, outlining plans for a shared Cardano presence at twelve conferences across twelve cities. Published on 4 November, the proposal requests USD 4,999,155 to support the execution of the global events programme, including a funded side event or hackathon at each stop and travel support for selected builders. The proposal also makes clear that the Cardano Foundation will not charge for staff time or take a cut of the requested funds. The proposal includes an overview of previous event activities, covering 20 events from Blockchain.RIO in August 2025 to WebX Asia in July 2026. The reported figures include 219 collaborations, 50 of which involved government and regulatory bodies, 8,191 booth contacts, 1,169 developers engaged and 79 projects given a stage. With the proposal now up for consideration, two AMA sessions were held on 9 November, giving DReps an opportunity to raise questions and discuss the plans. The recording of Session 2 is available on YouTube , while the consolidated Q&A from both sessions has also been published on the Cardano Forum. November SPO Call Summary, by Rick McCracken Community member Rick McCracken shared a summary of the 5 November SPO call , with one update in particular worth keeping an eye on: node 11.3, expected in December, will include Linear Leios capability. There is still some testing and tuning to do on testnet, so the rollout is taking a gradual approach. Performance will be monitored as the ecosystem works towards the throughput improvements Leios is expected to bring. In a follow-up post , Rick shared another interesting detail: Linear Leios will initially run at a lower setting, with capacity gradually increased as the balance between performance and costs is assessed. Want to stay in the loop for upcoming SPO calls? You can sign up via the Luma page to receive an update as soon as a new session is scheduled. The Hard Fork Working Group also publishes minutes from every session for those who prefer to keep up with the discussions in writing. Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates Robert Phair ’s latest CIP snapshot zooms in on the mechanics behind Cardano’s next chapter. Dynamic Rewards, on-chain governance role declarations and a Dijkstra-era web-wallet bridge join the pipeline as new candidates, while three substantial proposals move into active review and no CIPs reached completion. New Proposals CIP-0207 candidate: Dynamic Rewards - a re-formulation of this CIP-0163 component as a separate proposition (see discussion ): of great interest to stake pool operators and those following potential changes to Cardano’s proof-of-stake and reward mechanisms. CIP-0208 candidate: Disclosure of Governance Roles - a means of producing & interpreting machine-readable, on-chain declarations for governance actors (stake pools, DReps, or Constitutional Committee members), providing an alternative to error-prone social media and web sites. CIP-0209 candidate: Web-Wallet Bridge - Dijkstra era - including a “Balance, sign and submit” extension for improved developer experience and user efficiency - with a potentially expanded scope of new wallet primitives taking advantage of Cardano features in the new Ledger era. Active review Three new proposals representing substantial development effort, though not yet confirmed: DRep Groups - higher-level structure for creating and managing membership groups of DReps: headed for current implementation while seeking confirmation from governance / analytics tooling providers and community members. Layer 1 Data Availability - a CPS outlining a solution scope for integrated large-data handling systems on the Cardano chain: including native authenticity proofs and security guarantees. Nested Transactions - Service Layer - Light Clients - an expansion of the proposed Service Layer ( candidate CIP-0198 ) to provide detailed knowledge of partial transactions as they are submitted for conditional execution. Completed None this period. Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates The latest Cardanians ecosystem newsletter, Cardano Newsletter #148 , went out on X on 9 November. Here’s a taste of what’s inside: Cardano PRIME has begun onboarding DeFi projects with a goal of $200M+ in DeFi TVL over twelve months through grants, incentives and integrations; the ecosystem passed 127 million mainnet transactions; and Carlos Lopez de Lara shared a video on the Leios rollout. All this and more in their Ecosystem update. Check it out! Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #151 Lucas’ Weekly Cardano Digest also landed on 9 November, with Issue #151 covering a few interesting developments. Midnight’s Ledger 9 went live on mainnet on 6 November, bringing native ECDSA and Keccak-256 support alongside direct contract-to-contract interaction. Input Output also took the privacy conversation to institutional audiences at SALT, while Lace 2.5 introduced the ability to generate DUST from the cNIGHT held in users’ Cardano accounts, all within one wallet. There’s more to explore in the full issue, so head over to Lucas’ website to catch up and also subscribe. Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators Two explainers caught my attention this fortnight, both offering a closer look at developments that are worth keeping an eye on. On 5 November, Pete Bui, better known as astroboysoup, published an eight-minute walkthrough of the entire PRIME cohort . He goes through the participating teams, what they’re building and some of the gaps that still exist across Cardano DeFi. Along the way, he also touches on an important distinction: while funding helps get projects off the ground, building sustainable products, delivering on the technical side and attracting liquidity are very different challenges. Another topic getting attention is the upcoming Dijkstra era. On 4 November, Carlos Lopez de Lara shared a Dijkstra era explainer , aimed at Constitutional Committee members, DReps and SPOs. It walks through the rollout, the different roles involved and the steps that need to be taken along the way, including the constitutional amendment. Carlos also outlines three calls to action: join the discussion in the Constitutional Amendment Portal, vote yes on the constitution update when it comes to a vote, and vote yes on the hard fork action. For anyone following the preparations for Dijkstra, it’s a useful overview alongside the underlying governance discussions and CAP-12. Community Learning & Developer Engagement Moving over to the developer side, Developers Office Hours #86 took place on 6 November, with BlockSign founder Dennis Mittmann joining the session. The discussion covered BlockSign’s experience implementing CIP-0113, institutional asset operations, regulated stablecoins and the role of MCP in controlled agentic payments. The session thread includes the outline, with the recording to follow on the Cardano Developers playlist. There’s another session coming up on 13 November. Developers Office Hours #87 will feature Yano X, exploring the topic of trust you can verify. You can find the session details here . There’s also a Governance Hour worth catching up on. On 5 November, Nicolas Cerny sat down with Rahul Konudula, founder of Trivolve Tech, for Governance Hour #13: Deep Dive Into PFMS – Bringing Government Scale Adoption to Cardano . The discussion looks at the proposed Police Force Management System (PFMS), including its technical implementation, expected network activity, funding milestones and independent oversight. Building on Trivolve Tech’s existing forensic management system in Uttar Pradesh, the proposal looks at extending evidence tracking across different stages of the police and judicial process, with an initial deployment planned in Telangana, India. The proposal requests 9.6 million ada from the Treasury, with voting scheduled to end on 20 November 2026 (start of Epoch 669) . And there’s more on the governance calendar this week. The Intersect Product Committee meets on 11 November, followed by the CAP Review on 12 November, where editors work through proposals and review their progress in the open. Both sessions are listed on the Cardano Events calendar . Updates from the Cardano Foundation There’s been quite a bit happening across the ecosystem over the past ten days, with developments in tokenized assets, real-world applications, university partnerships, zero-knowledge research and a new group of teams joining the Cardano Accelerator. Let’s start with Switzerland. On 29 October, the Cardano Foundation became a member of CMTA , the Geneva-based association setting standards for tokenized capital markets. This follows CMTA’s recognition of CIP-0113 as equivalent to its CMTAT framework. In practical terms, issuers can now use Cardano’s standard for certifiable shares, while the Foundation gets a seat at the table where these standards are being shaped. The committee decision is publicly available for those interested in the finer details. Moving across the Atlantic, Latin America brought another interesting development. On 4 November, the Foundation shared that Petrobras is tokenizing sustainable aviation fuel certificates on Cardano. LATAM Business Development Lead Rafael Fraga also joined Petrobras on CNN Brasil to discuss how blockchain-based traceability works in practice, including how retiring a token helps prevent the same sustainability claim from being counted twice. There’s also a SAF case study that goes into the technical side of the implementation. And speaking of real-world applications, there are two more case studies worth a look, alongside some activity on the education front. The TrivolveTech FMS case study looks at how Uttar Pradesh police replaced a shared case ID with individual identifiers for each handler. Every scan and lab result is hashed to Cardano, helping maintain accountability and traceability throughout the chain of custody. Education is also part of that picture. During the week of 19 October, the Foundation’s partnership with UCLA moved into the classroom, with a masterclass, a four-hour session, a five-hour accelerator workshop and the Draper Innovation Showcase , sponsored by the Foundation. There’s more to come, too, with curriculum content expected to follow in 2027. On the technical side, there’s some reading to catch up on. On 10 November, Pawel Jakubas published Zero Knowledge Proof from First Principles to Production , the first instalment in a five-part series. It starts with the intuition behind zk-SNARKs and works its way towards generating and verifying a Groth16 proof inside a Plutus script, without relying on black boxes. The next instalments will cover optimisation, key ownership, selective disclosure and lattice-based systems. A slightly shorter read, if you’re more interested in the institutional side of programmable tokens, is The Rules Guiding Your Financial Assets , which takes about five minutes. And a couple of other things before we move on. Reeve shipped release 1.8, bringing improvements to project lifecycle reporting. Meanwhile, the Fall 2026 Cardano Accelerator cohort kicked off in Dublin. Eight teams are now working on projects spanning verification, identity and traceability, with Demo Day scheduled for 3 February 2027. Intersect Updates Intersect has also been busy over the past two weeks, with quite a bit happening around the 2027 budget process, Dijkstra readiness and ongoing governance discussions. Let’s start with the 2027 budget. In update #135, Shaping 2027 , Intersect outlined a proposed Cardano Ecosystem Budget Process (CEBP), developed together with the Cardano Foundation and other ecosystem stakeholders. The idea is to organise treasury requests around seven budget domains, each with a designated steward responsible for developing a strategy, suggesting a budget cap and helping bring comparable proposals to DReps. There’s also an Open Contributions domain, which allows anyone to submit proposals directly to DReps without going through a steward. DReps retain the final say on all funding decisions, and any domains that don’t receive approval would fall under Open Contributions. The proposed process would run as a trial in 2027, with feedback currently being gathered through DRepTalk or the Cardano Forum thread . On the technical side, DijkstraNet has now made the move to protocol version 12. The hard fork took place on 2 November, opening up testing of the Dijkstra-era features for developers, wallet providers and infrastructure teams. Intersect followed this up with Upgrade Bulletin #41 on 4 November, covering the network upgrade and the release of DB-Sync 13.8.0.0, which operators across Preview, Preprod and Mainnet are advised to update to. Node 11.2 is currently intended for DijkstraNet testing, while 11.2.1 is expected to bring mainnet clearance and a fix for a memory usage regression. Node 11.3 is planned to bring the full Dijkstra feature set, including Linear Leios. The Hard Fork Working Group minutes from 3 and 10 November provide a closer look at the ongoing discussions around releases, readiness, scope and node diversity. There’s also been some movement on the constitutional side. Intersect’s update #136 reports that CAP-12, covering Dijkstra-era parameters, has reached version 5, with around thirty parameter values still awaiting feedback from the Parameter Committee. Other amendments are progressing at different speeds: CAP-10 reached version 4, CAP-9 reached version 3, while CAP-3 has seen no new version since 21 October. CAP-1, CAP-2, CIS-4 and CIS-11 are also waiting for responses to outstanding reviewer questions. The next CAP Review takes place on 12 November, and all proposals and discussions can be followed through the Constitutional Amendment Portal . A couple of things are worth keeping in mind if you’re involved in Cardano governance. Intersect’s Civics Committee is encouraging ada holders to check whether their current DRep is still active and whether their voting record reflects their views. Tools such as DRepTalk , CGOV and Learn Cardano can help with that. The Intersect Annual Members Meeting is also coming up in the week of 7 December. This year’s meeting will be spread across three online sessions: 7 December for the Board, leadership and committee updates, 9 December for member questions and discussion, and 10 December for a global community connect day across different time zones. Finally, Intersect Executive Director Jack Briggs also spoke with NIKKEI Financial about the convergence of traditional finance and DeFi, and how trust, resilience and security fit into the next phase of institutional blockchain adoption. Fred Tanaka shared the interview on X . Cardano Forum Top 10 Referred Topics Topics that have received the most clicks from external sources. items.title: Cardano Global Events 2027: A Proposal for the Ecosystem
items.description: Conferences are where builders, enterprises, investors, and regulators decide which ecosystems to work with. In 2025-2026, one shared Cardano presence at these events started 219 collaborations, including 50 with government and regulatory bodies, engaged 1,169 developers, and gave 79 Cardano projects a stage most could not afford on their own. Cardano Global Events 2027 is the proposal to keep that presence in place for 2027. In September, the Cardano Foundation outlined its plans for Cardano Global Events 2027 in the catch-up post on the Cardano Forum . Based on community feedback, those plans have now become a full Treasury withdrawal proposal, shaped by a year of results from the first unified events program. The proposal requests US$4,999,155 to give Cardano one shared presence at 12 major industry conferences between January and December 2027. Each conference comes with a funded side event or hackathon, and the budget pays for selected builders to travel and take part. The request stays within the US$5 million upper limit proposed in September, and the Foundation will not charge for its staff time or make any profit from the proposal. Cardano Global Events 2027 seeks to renew the 2025-2026 Unified Global Events Marketing Strategy that met or exceeded every target . The full proposal is available here: https://ucarecdn.com/bf2042db-6907-430c-9efb-33281147e486/ Why It Matters Conferences are where Cardano builders do business. A shared booth gives projects a place to demonstrate their products, meet partners and investors, and speak to regulators, at events many could not attend alone. Unlike broad awareness campaigns, each activation reports against its own targets, so DReps can see what every event delivered. Without a funded program, Cardano would return to a fragmented presence: fewer projects at the events that matter, and no shared space for builders to do business from, at conferences where other layer 1 ecosystems are present. A Year of Results to Build On The 2025-2026 Unified Global Events Marketing Strategy was the first time Cardano took one coordinated presence to the world’s major industry events. Delivered by the Cardano Foundation, EMURGO, and Rare Network, and approved with nearly 70% support from delegated representatives (DReps), the program ran from Blockchain.RIO in August 2025 to WebX Asia in Tokyo in July 2026. Across 20 activities, it gave 79 Cardano projects a stage. The Treasury-funded program met or exceeded every target in its proposal, with 8,191 booth contacts and 1,169 developers engaged. The final results for each event are published here: https://ucarecdn.com/58a248dc-2003-4731-ba17-68979fb30d5a/EXT_BoothProposal2025KPIS3_September_2026_FINAL_CardanoBoothResults.pdf The 2027 Program The 2027 program takes the same model into a full calendar year, with more support for the builders who make each booth worth visiting. Every activation includes: a Cardano-branded booth shared with participating ecosystem projects, a funded side event: a hackathon, workshop, or networking session (four hackathons across the year, plus Dev Gov Day at Rare Evo), a speaking slot for Cardano content, where the sponsorship package includes one and subject to availability, media outreach before and during the event. Quarter Event Location Dates Side event Q1 Africa Tech Summit 2027 Nairobi, Kenya 10-11 February 2027 Hackathon Q2 TEAMZ Summit 2027 Tokyo, Japan 6-7 April 2027 Workshop Q2 Money20/20 Asia 2027 Bangkok, Thailand 27-29 April 2027 Networking Q2 Consensus Miami 2027 Miami, United States 4-6 May 2027 Workshop Q2 TOKEN2049 New York 2027 New York, United States 16-17 June 2027 Hackathon Q3 Signal Week 2027 (formerly Paris Blockchain Week) Paris, France 6-7 July 2027 Networking Q3 Rare Evo 2027 San Francisco, United States 13-15 August 2027 Dev Gov Day Q4 TOKEN2049 Singapore 2027 Singapore October 2027 Networking Q4 LABITCONF 2027 Buenos Aires, Argentina November 2027 Hackathon Q4 Australian Crypto Convention 2027 Sydney, Australia November 2027 Workshop Q4 Web Summit 2027 Lisbon, Portugal November 2027 Networking Q4 India Blockchain Week 2027 Bangalore, India December 2027 Hackathon A few changes to note from the last catch-up post, following ecosystem feedback and changes in locations from event organizers. The calendar has grown from 11 to 12 conferences: Web Summit in Lisbon joins the program, TOKEN2049 New York replaces Digital Asset Summit NYC, TEAMZ Summit takes the Tokyo slot, and Rare Evo moves to San Francisco in August. Why Now With the first program complete, the window to secure 2027 is already open. Major conferences sell sponsorship packages and the best booth positions months in advance, and events of this size typically need at least six months of preparation. Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi opens the calendar on 10-11 February 2027, less than four months away. If the community approve this proposal only in 2027, it could cover only half of the events planned in the same calendar year. Advance planning is needed and will lead to better negotiation, early pricing, and bulk vendor deals for the most cost-effective option. Approving the proposal now lets us lock in sponsorship packages and booth space for Cardano while they are still available, and gives builders time to apply for travel support, visas and plan their launches around the calendar. If ratification comes later, early activations such as Nairobi in February may need to be dropped or replaced, and any funds not spent return to the Treasury under the proposal’s withdrawal terms. How This Fits the 2027 Ecosystem Budget Process On 28 October 2026, Intersect published a concept for how treasury funding could work for 2027: the Cardano Ecosystem Budget Process (CEBP) . It groups ecosystem needs into funding domains, each with a steward, a strategy and a budget cap that DReps approve before withdrawals are submitted. Events, such as those covered by this proposal, would sit in the Marketing, Analysis & Events domain. We have worked on this concept together with Intersect and other ecosystem stakeholders and have put ourselves forward as a potential steward of the Marketing, Analysis & Events domain. We believe we have experience and a track record to deliver on a strategy for this domain, working with other ecosystem partners to establish a cohesive Cardano presence around the globe. If DReps approve the CEBP direction and the Foundation as a potential steward, we will share a comprehensive strategy for DRep approval in Stage 3 of CEBP (see the Intersect post for more information). We envision that the CEBP and this Global Events 2027 proposal could run in parallel. This is necessitated by timing concerns, with 2027 fast approaching and the need to plan events in advance, as outlined above. Waiting would mean higher prices and, for the first events of the year, no Cardano presence at all. These are opportunities the ecosystem should not give up while a new process is being set up. If this proposal is approved, we envision that it would fall under the Marketing, Analysis & Events domain and be deducted from the budget cap DReps approve for that domain. This could apply even if a different steward is chosen for this domain. The ecosystem would pay for these events once and it would be fully consistent with the new CEBP. If the CEBP is not approved, this Global Events 2027 proposal could still operate standalone, similarly to the 2026 round of treasury withdrawals. Four Core Principles The following principles underpin the entire Cardano Global Events 2027 strategy: 1. Builders come first. The program exists to put Cardano projects in front of developers, users, partners, and investors at conferences many could not afford to attend alone, with space to showcase at the booth and their travel paid for. 2. Clear accountability, local delivery. The Cardano Foundation remains responsible for delivery and results. In Africa, Latin America, the United States, and Australia, it works with local ecosystem partners and Cardano Ambassadors who know those regions. Where a local partner delivers an activation, the partner’s fee of 10% of event costs is shown in that event’s budget. 3. Aligned with the Cardano 2030 Strategy. The program serves three aims of the Strategy. It reaches Latin America, Africa, and East Asia, the priority markets named in Pillar 4 , through events in Buenos Aires, Nairobi, and Tokyo. It shows Cardano’s value in public, building on 147 articles and broadcast interviews in 2025-2026. The program also helps grow a skilled developer base, after engaging 1,169 developers last year, through four hackathons and a route into the Cardano Developer Portal and the Cardano Academy. 4. A calendar the ecosystem can plan around. Twelve activations run from January to December, with dates published a year ahead, so projects can time launches and announcements to the events where their audiences will be. Support for Builders Ecosystem Travel Support is for builders who would not otherwise be able to attend. The Cardano Foundation will open calls on the Forum ahead of each quarter’s events, and any team building on Cardano with a product live on mainnet may apply. Availability for demonstration slots at the booth and ability to report on outcomes afterward are key criteria for applicants. The Foundation will run the selection process in consultation with the Intersect Growth and Marketing Committee. Support covers economy travel and accommodation, booked directly by the Foundation or reimbursed against receipts. Projects must accept the Foundation’s terms and conditions, including identity checks (KYC), to receive support. The final report names every project supported and the amount paid. Selection does not constitute an endorsement by the Cardano Foundation of any project, product, or token. Budget and Safeguards The total request is US$4,999,155 (24,995,775 ada at an assumed rate of US$0.20 per ada), including audit fees and taxes. The full draft proposal sets out the cost of every event. This is an estimate based on current planning and dependencies, as set out more fully in the full draft proposal. What it pays for US$ Side events at all 12 conferences, including four hackathons 695,000 Sponsorship packages: speaking slots, tickets, and floor space 1,989,000 Booth build and audio-visual (AV) 1,060,000 Travel for participating builders and staff 702,000 Merchandise 82,000 Local partner fees at six events 233,100 Taxes, Audit & other fees (5%) 238,055 Total 4,999,155 The 2027 targets include 9,520 booth contacts, 137 workshops and builder presentations, and 4,750 side-event registrations. The full set of KPIs is in the draft proposal, and the final report will set results against every target. Importantly, this budget and the list of planned events is dependent on the timing of approval of the proposal and final pricing from vendors. If the treasury withdrawal for events is approved later than the end of December 2026, then the final list of events may need to be adjusted to obtain best value-for-money and exposure within the original intent of the program. What the Community Gets Builders gain a stage, paid travel, and an audience many could not reach on their own budgets. The Treasury gets published spend for every event and the return of any funds that go unused. Local Cardano communities get a funded side event in their region, with targets of 860 Cardano community attendees and 1,290 people from outside the ecosystem, and Cardano Ambassadors help deliver activations in the regions they know. The wider ecosystem gets a consistent Cardano presence at the conferences where developers, partners, and investors already gather, with a yearly record of what that presence achieved. Next Steps Major conferences book space and sponsorships months in advance, so we respectfully present this proposal to DReps for your consideration and vote, in hopes of securing the 2027 calendar. The first activation is Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi on 10-11 February 2027, and the governance action is planned to go on-chain in November 2026. Questions and feedback are welcome in this thread. The Foundation will host two DRep sessions on Monday 9 November 2026, so DReps in every time zone can join: 10:00 to 11:00 CET: https://www.addevent.com/event/kg7fq2gbl2bq 17:00 to 18:00 CET: https://www.addevent.com/event/pwkl3964x67m Each link adds the session to your calendar with the joining details. We ask DReps to vote yes, and we ask community members who support the proposal to tell their DRep. items.description: Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: State of the Cardano Developer Ecosystem Survey: The Cardano Foundation’s 2026 survey invites developers and builders to share feedback on Cardano’s tools, libraries, documentation and resources. Responses will be recorded on-chain, with the survey open until November 30. Leios & Dijkstra Testnet: Input Output outlined a staged rollout for Leios, targeting 3–5x current throughput initially, with later parameter updates aiming for 10–15x. The public Dijkstra testnet is now open to SPOs. IOG Research: Five new papers explore cross-chain security, consensus, post-quantum cryptography, privacy-preserving governance and the long-term economics of Proof-of-Stake networks. CIP Updates: New proposals cover regulatable stablecoins and post-quantum signature verification, while two proposals have been completed, including CIP-0204 on holder answers to governance actions. Ecosystem Highlights: Cardano PRIME announced its first nine funded teams, Midnight expanded its privacy ambitions across other networks, and Cardano Dev Skills v2 is in development. Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators: Catch up on explainers about nodes, stake pools and scaling, a closer look at bringing Bitcoin into Cardano DeFi through Bifrost, and practical guides to Cardano wallets and Midnight. Community Learning & Developer Engagement: Sessions explore automated payments with x402, the new Cardano Research Exchange, and a hands-on Hydra technical workshop. Cardano Foundation Updates: 5am.earth’s agricultural data project has registered 100,000 farms in India on Cardano. The Foundation also shared its response to the EU’s MiCA consultation, announced a Cardano Academy collaboration with the University of Nicosia, and published a case study on blockchain-backed police evidence management. Intersect & Governance Updates: Intersect returned 115,172 ada in unspent funds to the Cardano treasury, shared updates on Dijkstra readiness and the upcoming Node Diversity Workshop, and highlighted three active treasury withdrawal proposals, including the ₳22 million Cardano Strategic Copper Reserve. All this and more in today’s Digest. CTA: State of the Cardano Developer Ecosystem Survey Heads Up Cardano Builders! The Cardano Foundation has now opened the 2026 State of the Cardano Developer Ecosystem survey . Here is an opportunity to share your experience and help shape the developer tooling and resources you rely on daily. Whether you’re developing DApps, writing smart contracts, running a stake pool or working with Cardano in another capacity, the survey looks to gather feedback on everything from libraries and SDKs to documentation and developer tooling. And the good thing about this is that it only takes around 15 minutes to complete and is available in nine languages. Pretty neat, right?! There’s also something new this year: survey responses will be permanently recorded on-chain and linked to an Info Action. Yes, you read that correctly! “survey responses will be permanently recorded on-chain”. Note that the survey will remain open until 30 November 2026. So if you’re building on Cardano, take a few minutes to share your experience. The feedback really does help decide future engineering priorities, and who better to contribute than the people working with these tools firsthand? Have your say at devsurvey.cardano.org . Leios Is Coming: A Staged Rollout, and the Public Dijkstra Testnet Is Open Input Output recently shared a detailed look at how Leios will make its way to Cardano mainnet. The Dijkstra hard fork is the starting point, with capacity increasing in stages as mainnet performance is tested and validated. The initial target is 3–5 times today’s throughput, with later parameter updates aiming for 10–15 times. The rollout involves five steps, from constitutional guardrails and the hard fork to SPO registration of BLS voting keys, mainnet load testing and capacity increases. Endorser blocks and committee voting will help Cardano handle higher transaction demand without slowing regular transactions. And if you’re curious to dig deeper into the details, then perhaps its good to note that the public Dijkstra testnet is officially up and running on node version 11.1.3, featuring accelerated one-day epochs alongside access to the Kleioscan explorer. Stake pool operators can jump in and begin onboarding by leveraging the setup configurations available directly within the Cardano Book. Read the full Leios rollout overview and Intersect’s Dijkstra testnet update for the details. IOG Research: Five New Papers Published in October IOG researchers published five new papers this October, covering topics ranging from cross-chain security and consensus mechanics to post-quantum cryptography, privacy-preserving governance and the long-term economics of Proof-of-Stake networks. The research explores how blockchain bridges can be formally tested for security, how GHOST consensus behaves under adversarial conditions, and how cryptographic key sharing can remain secure without relying on the irreversible deletion of old key shares. Another paper looks at privacy-preserving opinion aggregation, with potential applications in on-chain polls and decentralised governance. The fifth examines how PoS networks can maintain economic security as token reserves decline and transaction fees take on a greater role. Five different research questions, each touching on challenges that matter for the long-term security, scalability and sustainability of blockchain systems. Explore the individual papers and their findings via the IOG Research Library . Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates This week, Robert Phair ’s snapshot is all about future-proofing Cardano. Regulatable stablecoins and quantum-resistant smart contracts are on the table, governance metadata is getting a best practice guide, and two proposals have been completed. New Proposals (CPS draft) Standardisation of Regulatable Stablecoins - so far tracking 2 problem statement submissions — one focusing on compliance concerns across jurisdictions, and one prefacing technical solutions for discovery of new programmable token features. CIP-0206 candidate: Post-Quantum Signature Verification Builtins - another submitted potential signature scheme to provide quantum resistance at the level of Plutus smart contracts. Active Review (issue) Interaction & discoverability of governance metadata schemes - evolving the need for a “best practice” document explaining how the layered metadata & property schemas for Cardano’s on-chain governance components are extended and interpreted. Completed CIP-0204 | Holder Answers on Governance Actions CPS-0037 | Application and transaction friction in minUTxO implementation Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates Cardanians. Cardano Newsletter #146 went out on 26 October as a nine-post thread on X. Three teasers: Cardano PRIME announced its first nine funded teams in the 12-month, ₳120M DeFi program; Midnight’s “Nightmode” extends privacy features to Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron; and Cardano Dev Skills v2 is in development with support for Claude, Codex and Cursor. Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #149 Lucas Macchiavelli released Weekly Cardano Digest #149 on October 19. Highlights include Intersect returning unspent operational budget, the on-chain registration of 100,000 Indian agricultural plots using Cardano metadata, and the latest Project Catalyst pilot selecting 12 projects for a 2 million ada fund. Read the complete issue on the Weekly Cardano Digest #149 Page . . Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators This week, there’s quite a lot to catch up on across the Cardano content scene. From wallet guides and Midnight tutorials to Bitcoin integrations and the next steps for Cardano DeFi. Definitely a nice mix of content this time around. The Cardano Record continued its Crypto from Zero series with two new explainers. Episode #7 , Who Runs Cardano? Nodes, Relays and Stake Pools Explained , published on 22 October, breaks down the different roles keeping the network running. Episode #8 followed on 24 October with How Blockchains Scale: Cardano’s Block Limits, Leios and Hydra , taking a closer look at the approaches being explored to scale Cardano. A good pairing if you’re keen to brush up on the basics and then dig a little deeper. Over at Builders Bench, Cardano Ambassador Peter Bui, better known as astroboysoup , sat down with FluidTokens to explore Bifrost . The interview looks at how Bifrost aims to bring Bitcoin into Cardano DeFi, including its approach to Bitcoin security and a walkthrough of the testnet. Definitely one for those curious about where Bitcoin and Cardano could meet beyond the usual conversations. Choosing a wallet shouldn’t require a research project of its own, and @Mb_you_know has put together a beginner’s guide to choosing a Cardano wallet . It compares options such as Lace, Eternl and Vespr, giving newcomers a starting point for figuring out which wallet works best for them. For the Midnight crowd, Gero Wallet shared a tutorial on generating DUST and sending NIGHT . It walks through the practical steps involved, making it a useful resource for anyone looking to get familiar with the process rather than just reading about it. Last but certainly not least, Cardano Prime hosted a live session on Cardano DeFi and the founders working towards $200 million in TVL on 27 October. Joining were teams from its first cohort - all working across DEX infrastructure, lending, automated liquidity, bridges, real-world assets and on-chain payments. What makes this session interesting is the fact that you now get to hear directly from the teams about what they’re building and the gaps they’re trying to address. After all, growing TVL is one thing; building the infrastructure and user experience that give people a reason to stick around is another. Definitely Worth a watch. Community Learning & Developer Engagement A bit of everything for those looking to learn something new across the Cardano ecosystem. This week’s selection covers automated payments, research, scaling and developer tooling. Some useful sessions to catch up on, whether you’re building on Cardano or simply curious about what’s happening under the hood. x402: Build, Pay, Automate with Thomas Kammerlocher: What happens when software and AI agents can pay for services without someone having to approve every transaction? In this developer session, Thomas Kammerlocher breaks down the x402 payment protocol and how it can be used with Cardano to enable automated, on-chain payments. The session explores how services can request payments through standard HTTP responses and how this could open the door to new kinds of autonomous workflows. Watch the full session on YouTube or on X . Cardano Research Exchange #1: The Cardano Foundation recently launched the Research Exchange. The aim is to create a space where researchers and anyone contributing to Cardano research can present their work, engage directly with the Cardano Community, exchange ideas, and receive live feedback to help challenge, refine, and further develop their research. The first session introduced research initiatives at the Foundation, including mathematical and economic modelling around staking incentives and minimum pool parameters. Catch the full session on YouTube and on X . Hydra Technical Workshop: Curious about how Hydra works beyond the theory? This technical workshop with the Hydra engineering team gets into the practical side of Cardano scaling, covering Hydra Heads, state channels, the interaction with Layer 1 and how to set up a local environment for dApp development. A useful one for developers who want to get their hands dirty and explore how Hydra could fit into their applications. Watch the workshop and Q&A on YouTube or check out the X version . Updates from the Cardano Foundation **The Cardano Foundation has put out a handful of updates in the last ten days, spanning its stance on EU crypto regulation, new Cardano Academy partnerships with universities, and Cardano-backed projects tracking farmland in India and police evidence in Uttar Pradesh. ** On October 21, the Foundation announced that 100,000 farms in India are now registered on Cardano through 5am.earth’s agricultural data project. As outlined in the Syngenta Foundation India case study , the project gives each farm a digital identity tied to satellite-verified land boundaries, so banks, insurers and agribusinesses can check records independently. That is a big jump from roughly 15,000 farms reported in June. crypto An X Space has also been scheduled for October 28th at 14:00 UTC. Use the following link to join live, or re-listen at a later moment The same day, also on October 21st, the Foundation published its response to the European Commission’s public consultation on MiCA . The post argues that more regulation does not necessarily mean better regulation, and focuses on keeping a clear boundary between MiCAR and existing financial-services rules such as MiFID II. cardanofoundation On October 22, the Foundation announced a new Cardano Academy collaboration with the University of Nicosia. According to the announcement on X , the Academy will teach Cardano fundamentals and the eUTxO model in the university’s online blockchain course, and the Foundation is sponsoring 25 places in the advanced track. Registration closes on November 2, and the course starts on February 8, 2027. crypto Finally, on October 26, the Foundation shared a new case study from Uttar Pradesh. Every scan and lab result is hashed on-chain, live on active cases. The TrivolveTech FMS case study explains how the system was built to remove the case identifier that makes evidence tampering possible. Intersect MBO Updates In its Weekly Update #134, “Receipts” , Intersect shared that it had executed the SweepTreasury function on mainnet for the first time, returning 115,172 ada in unspent funds from its 2025 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract to the Cardano treasury. You can find the announcement on X . The newsletter also covers the latest CAP updates and upcoming workshops. Executive Director Jack Briggs discussed the idea of “one member, one vote” in a recording from TOKEN2049 , while Intersect shared an interview with Cardano Foundation’s Josi , recorded at the Intersect booth. On the governance front, Update 39 covers the opening of the Dijkstra testnet to SPOs and shares details about the upcoming Node Diversity Workshop. As of 22 October, three treasury withdrawal actions were live: the Cardano Strategic Copper Reserve, requesting ₳22 million for RWA tokenization, and the AURORA and Trivolve Tech PFMS proposals. The Copper Reserve action closes on 15 November, while the other two close on 20 November. The Cardano Strategic Copper Reserve proposal was also the focus of the 27 October episode of Governance Hour, where Toto Finance’s CEO sat down with Nicolas Cerny, Governance Lead at the Cardano Foundation, to take a closer look at the proposal and its ₳22 million treasury request. If you missed the live discussion, you can catch the recording on YouTube or X . Cardano Forum Top 10 Referred Topics Topics that have received the most clicks from external sources. items.description: Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: TOKEN2049 Singapore Recap: Cardano brought 20+ ecosystem projects to its 108 m² booth, welcomed 2,000+ visitors, and co-organized a Rooftop UTXO Pitch Night with Draper Dragon, with up to $500,000 in funding on the table. CIP-0113 Goes Live: Cardano’s programmable token standard is now live on mainnet, enabling compliance rules for regulated assets to be built directly into tokens. The Foundation’s Veridian project also issued its shares on-chain using the standard. Origins Hackathon: Around 200 builders took part in the TOKEN2049 hackathon, with the Cardano track attracting around 130 developers. Three winning projects explored AI agent payments, real-world purchases, and private funding. Open Wallet Standard: Introduces native Cardano support, including transaction signing and policy-based controls for AI agents. Ambassador Stories: Meet Ian McCullough, aka Cullah, a musician and creative producer who found his way into Cardano through music rights, Project Catalyst, and a growing interest in governance. CIP Updates: New and active proposals cover block producer payloads, programmable token custody and issuance, and potential changes to CIP-0068. CIP-0195, covering Plutus V4 ledger type encoding, has been completed. Cardano Foundation Updates: Highlights include blockchain initiatives with Petrobras, a partnership with Pacific Meta in Japan, a UCLA blockchain education collaboration, and progress on the .ada top-level domain application. Intersect & Governance Updates: Intersect highlights Dijkstra preparations, an open SPO poll on increasing the target number of stake pools, and continued protocol development. SPOs and node operators are also reminded that node 11.1.2 is the minimum version, with 11.1.3 recommended. All this and more in today’s Digest. Cardano’s Presence at Token2049 2026 Singapore - Recap With TOKEN2049 now behind us, it’s time to look back at what was a strong couple of days for Cardano in Singapore. Thanks to Treasury funding approved by DReps, Cardano had a 108 m² booth bringing together more than 20 ecosystem projects. Over the two days, more than 2,000 visitors stopped by to explore what the ecosystem is building and hear the case for trust as blockchain’s defining advantage. Missed some of the action? The Cardano X account shared a recap after each day, covering some of the highlights from the conference. Catch up with the Day 1 recap and Day 2 recap . And if you want a closer look at what was happening at the booth, Cardano Ambassador Peter Bui also shared a walkthrough on X . Of course, there was plenty happening beyond the booth, too. The Cardano Foundation co-organized a Rooftop UTXO Pitch Night with Draper Dragon, bringing together 90+ investors, nine teams, and more than 400 attendees , with up to $500,000 in funding on the table. A pretty good mix of builders, investors, and ideas in one room! If you missed it, here’s a short MUST WATCH, high energy clip reflecting the highlights of the evening. Click here to watch it . And it wasn’t just us saying the booth had a great atmosphere. Patrick Tobler shared his take in a post on X , describing it as the best booth at TOKEN2049, with a great location, plenty of energy, and visitors stopping by throughout the event. Those are just a few highlights from a busy few days. Below are some of the notable announcements and developments that came out of TOKEN2049. Programmable Tokens (CIP-0113) Are Live on Cardano Mainnet On October 7, the Cardano Foundation announced that CIP-0113, Cardano’s programmable token standard, was live on mainnet. It allows issuers of stablecoins, tokenized funds, bonds and other regulated assets to build compliance rules directly into tokens. These can include identity verification, KYC and AML checks, sanctions screening, transfer restrictions, and freeze or seizure controls. The rules are enforced by the ledger whenever a token is transferred, minted or burned, without requiring a hard fork. In short, compliance rules can travel with the asset instead of relying solely on external systems. Read the launch announcement here The launch also brought recognition from the Swiss Capital Markets and Technology Association (CMTA), which considers CIP-0113 a smart-contract equivalent to its CMTAT framework for certification purposes. Support from ecosystem tools including Eternl , GeroWallet , CardanoScan and BloxBean also helps lay the groundwork for integrating programmable tokens into the tools people already use. Curious the see what they all had to share about this launch? And there is already a real-world example. Veridian, the Foundation’s digital identity project, became an independent Swiss company, with its shares issued on-chain using CIP-0113. Veridian plans to seek strategic partners and investors in 2027. The two developments address complementary parts of the trust equation: programmable tokens can carry the rules governing an asset, while verifiable digital credentials can help establish who is behind a transaction. Read the full announcement here Want to dig into what this means for regulated assets on Cardano? Tune into the upcoming live Roundtable Talk: “CIP-113: What Programmable Tokens Mean for Regulated Assets” on October 29 . Details and the link to join can be found here on Luma . Cardano Steals the Spotlight at TOKEN2049 Origins Hackathon Over 36 hours at the TOKEN2049 Origins Hackathon in Singapore, around 200 builders worked on projects across several blockchain ecosystems. According to the Cardano Foundation’s TOKEN2049 recap , the overall winner came from the dedicated Cardano track, where developers were challenged to build for the emerging agentic economy using x402. Around 130 of the 200 developers submitted projects to the Cardano track, either exclusively or alongside other tracks, using Cardano technology and interacting with the network to develop solutions to real-world problems. The track’s individual three winning projects focused on AI agents that can pay, get paid, and prove their work. CoinGraph took the overall grand prize across all tracks, building a verification layer that helps AI agents check information before moving funds. Cardano Card explored how AI agents could purchase real-world goods using Masumi Network escrow, while zx402 focused on private funding for autonomous agents using zero-knowledge proofs. Together, the projects offer a glimpse of how agentic commerce could develop on Cardano, from automated payments to privacy-conscious transactions. The hackathon was part of a wider TOKEN2049 programme, with teams building, testing, and presenting working ideas in a short space of time. For more on the results and the projects that came out of the event, check out the Cardano Foundation’s recap on X . Minswap and FluidTokens Join Forces on Cardano DeFi During TOKEN2049, Minswap and FluidTokens announced that they are joining forces, bringing together two established DeFi projects in the Cardano ecosystem. As shared in Linda’s post on X , the move brings Minswap’s decentralized exchange together with FluidTokens’ lending, borrowing, and NFT-backed DeFi services. FluidTokens CEO Matteo provided further context in a follow-up post on X , explaining that the projects will remain independent while sharing teams. According to Matteo, the collaboration aims to enable deeper integrations, higher yields, and greater liquidity, with a roadmap he believes could make Cardano more competitive in DeFi. For those who want to hear more directly from the teams, FluidTokens and Minswap have announced a joint X Space on October 20 at 09:00 UTC. The session will offer an opportunity to learn more about the plans and what comes next. Join the conversation on X . Linear Leios Is Coming. First, the Constitution. Cardano’s upcoming Dijkstra hard fork brings Ouroboros Linear Leios to mainnet. Linear Leios lets block producers publish larger endorser blocks alongside regular Praos blocks, so the network can process far more transactions without changing its security model. On Musashi Dojo , the public Leios testnet running since June 2026, the first test phase peaked at 26.8 TxkB/s against the 4.51 TxkB/s mainnet can handle today. That is roughly six times current capacity, with parameters still set conservatively. New features bring new protocol parameters, and the Cardano Constitution only lets governance change parameters that are listed in its Guardrails (Appendix I). Anything not listed stays frozen at its launch value. So before the Dijkstra hard fork goes to a vote, the Constitution needs an update that adds these parameters and sets safe ranges for each. That process has now started. A draft amendment is live on Intersect’s Constitutional Amendment Portal. It covers parameters for Leios, Peras, reference-script protection and two pool-reward changes (minimum pool margin and maximum pledge leverage), plus an updated Guardrails Script. Every change sits in Appendix I. The main body of the Constitution is untouched. Several guardrail values are still marked pending, so now is the time to review it and weigh in. Read the amendment: Constitutional Amendment Portal — Cardano Constitution Open Wallet Standard Adds Native Cardano Support The Open Wallet Standard (OWS) added native Cardano support with the release of v1.4.3. Developed by the WingRiders team, with technical coordination and review from Input Output Group (IOG) and the Midnight Foundation, the integration extends the open-source toolkit to support Cardano wallets and transaction signing. According to IOG’s announcement , OWS provides applications and AI agents with a shared interface for managing wallets and signing transactions. The integration adapts OWS to Cardano’s two-key structure under CIP-1852, where base addresses can contain a payment key for controlling funds and a stake key for delegation. The signer handles both keys independently, adding a stake-key signature when required for staking or delegation. Developers can also sign messages using base, enterprise, and reward addresses, and check balances through Koios APIs. The update introduces policy-based controls for AI agents signing Cardano transactions. Developers can assign API keys and define rules covering permitted networks, spending limits, and transaction expiration windows. OWS evaluates transaction details against these rules before approving a signature, giving developers more control over how autonomous agents interact with Cardano. Check out the announcement for the full technical update. Ambassador Stories, with Ian McCullough Meet Ian McCullough, also known as Cullah, one of the newest Ambassadors to join the Cardano Ambassador Program. Based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Ian wears quite a few hats: musician, creative producer, and blockchain advocate. His journey into Cardano started with a familiar frustration for independent artists: making music rights and royalty payments more transparent. That search led him to build Sync.Land and discover Project Catalyst, where he found something just as interesting as the technology itself: a community that helps decide how its resources are used - Governance! These days, Ian is deeply involved in Cardano governance through Intersect and the Curia consortium. He also brings Cardano into conversations with policymakers and the wider community. And he’s keen to show that you don’t need to be an engineer to make a difference. Sometimes, it starts with bringing the right people into the same room. His message to the community? Show up for the boring parts. The votes, discussions, and committee meetings might not grab the same attention as a price chart, but that’s where a lot of the important decisions happen. Curious how a musician from Milwaukee ended up helping shape Cardano governance? Read Ian’s full Ambassador Story here: https://forum.cardano.org/tag/ambassador-story/472 Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates Robert Phair ’s latest snapshot turns the spotlight on how existing standards hold up in practice, from a proposed path for tokens like USDM and USDA to achieve regulatory compliance through the programmable tokens standard, to a possible new version of CIP-0068 in response to the CF survey of real-world NFT data. New Proposals Block Producer Payloads - to provide more software details for each node type producing a block: either an extension to Block Producer Identifiers (candidate CIP-0203) or as a standalone CIP. Active Review Focusing primarily on ecosystem issues for existing CIPs in this period: CIP-0113: Separate programmable custody from issuance - to support existing CNTs and external mint/burn workflows - or any standardised process for existing tokens like USDM and USDA to achieve regulatory compliance through our newly launched “programmable tokens” standard. First up… Cardano recorded a new single-epoch record of 1,780,896 transactions, beating its previous record from November 2021, and has now surpassed 125 million mainnet transactions. Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #147 Another October 12 read: Lucas’s Weekly Cardano Digest #147 brings news on Plutus 1.71, now shipping Plutus V4 script capabilities, and Intersect’s rundown of the node releases needed for the upcoming Dijkstra hard fork. Two updates worth keeping on your radar if you’re following Cardano’s development. Full issue on https://www.cardanonewsletter.com/p/147 . Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators Plenty happening across the Cardano content scene this week, with community creators tackling everything from AI agent payments and liquid staking to stablecoins, wallet recovery, and protocol updates. Whether you’re looking to get up to speed on a new development or just want someone to break down the details without getting lost in the weeds, there’s a bit of everything in this week’s selection. The Cardano Record took a closer look at x402, the HTTP “Payment Required” status code, and how it could enable AI agents to pay for services on Cardano in AI Agents That Pay: x402, Cardano and Who Pays for the Internet . CryptoDossier shared a CIP-0113 explainer , while ItsDave_ADA put together a insightful visual tool that lets you explore Cardano block producer journeys . This last one is definitely worth a look for anyone curious about the infrastructure behind the network. Updates from the Cardano Foundation **The Cardano Foundation has shared several updates over the past two weeks, covering enterprise adoption, education, digital identity, internet infrastructure, and real-world applications of Cardano. ** On September 30, the Foundation announced two new blockchain initiatives developed with Brazilian energy company Petrobras and PUC-Rio’s Ledger Labs. According to the case study , the projects use Cardano to support the traceability of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable diesel. One applies a Book-and-Claim model to track environmental benefits, while the other records key stages in the renewable diesel supply chain. Both initiatives aim to make sustainability claims more transparent and verifiable. On October 1, the Foundation announced a partnership with Pacific Meta to support enterprise Web3 adoption in Japan. As outlined in the announcement on LinkedIn , the collaboration combines Cardano’s infrastructure with Pacific Meta’s local market presence and systems integration expertise, with the aim of helping Japanese businesses explore and implement blockchain solutions. Education was also on the agenda. On September 28, the Foundation announced a multi-year partnership with the Venture Accelerator at UCLA Anderson School of Management . The update highlights how the application follows a Cardano governance action that received about 75% stake weighted votes from the DReps. If approved, .ada could support simpler wallet addresses, digital identity integrations, and tokenized domains - something to definitely be excited about as it would enable connecting Cardano more closely with the wider internet. Finally, the Foundation’s September activities included CEO Frederik Gregaard’s participation in CV Summit in Zurich on September 29–30. The Foundation’s September monthly update highlights the event as part of its broader engagement with industry leaders around trust-based infrastructure and enterprise blockchain adoption. According to the Cardano Foundation’s Open Food Chain case study , the platform is using Cardano to anchor supply chain compliance data for brands including Kraft Heinz and Interfood, giving shoppers a way to trace product claims back to their source. Compliance paperwork might not sound exciting, but making that information useful to consumers is definitely an interesting one.
