items.title: Digest September 30: 9 Years of Cardano | CIP-113 Programmable Tokens Merged Into The CIP Repo | Cardano Node Update | TOKEN2049 Singapore | Developer Spotlight | Ecosystem & Governance Updates
items.description: ** ** Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: 9 Years of Cardano: Cardano celebrates nine years since its genesis block, with 2,890 stake pools, 123.98 million transactions, and 158 governance actions recorded. CIP-113: Programmable token-like assets have been merged into the main CIP repository, moving the standard into its next stage. Cardano Node 11.1.3: Intersect released a corrective node update fixing IPv4 address decoding. SPOs are encouraged to update, with no ledger replay required. TOKEN2049 Singapore: The Cardano Foundation is bringing a 108m² booth, 20 ecosystem projects, builder presentations, node diversity activities, and more to Singapore on October 7–8. Developer Spotlight: ODATANO creator Maximilian Weber explains how OData can make Cardano integration more accessible to enterprise and SAP developers. CIP Updates: Six new proposals cover trusted messaging, node observability, node signalling, governance actions, and Plutus Core, while CIP-113 has reached completion. Ecosystem & Creator Highlights: Cardanians covers Midnight, and Cardano DeFi, while creators look at Cardano, Midnight, research-driven development and recent ecosystem updates. Community Learning: Developer Office Hours explored Subbit.xyz and subscription payments, while the latest Roundtable looked at smart contract security and the impact of AI on auditing. CF & Intersect Updates: The Foundation announced a UCLA partnership, Barça Fan Lab launched on Cardano, Cardano joined the official x402 SDK, and Intersect announced its new Board members and Dijkstra preparations. All this and more in today’s Digest. 9 years of Cardano! September 23 marked nine years since Cardano’s genesis block was created, with the network subsequently moving through five eras: Byron, Shelley, Goguen, Basho and Voltaire. Each marked a major step in the network’s evolution, from the original Byron launch in September 2017, through Shelley’s decentralisation in July 2020, Goguen’s smart contract era, Basho’s focus on scalability, and finally Voltaire’s move toward community-led governance. An overview of the eras hardforks That governance journey has been quite something in itself. It moved from the CIP-1694 framework and a global series of constitutional workshops, to the first Constitutional Convention in Buenos Aires and Nairobi in December 2024, where delegates approved a draft Constitution. The process then moved on-chain, with the Constitution ultimately ratified by the Cardano community in February 2025. And the network today? The Foundation’s September 23 update counted 2,890 stake pools, 13.98 million blocks, 123.98 million transactions, and 36,322 votes across 158 governance actions. Nine years on, Cardano isn’t just marking another birthday. It has moved from building the network to building the mechanisms through which its community can govern it. Watch Here The Full Anniversary Video CIP-113 Programmable Tokens Merged Into The CIP Repo After years of work and review, the CIP-113 standard has now been merged into Cardano’s main CIP repository on September 29. This is an important step toward having programmable tokens on Cardano. The standard provides a framework for assets that can carry rules such as KYC allowlists, denylists, freezes, transfer limits or jurisdiction requirements, with those rules enforced on-chain whenever the asset moves. That could be particularly relevant for regulated assets and RWAs, where transfer rules are part of the asset itself. The news was quickly picked up across the ecosystem. Giovanni Gargiulo , who has played a central role in further developing and explaining the programmable-token work at the Cardano Foundation, highlighted the many contributors behind the effort and specifically thanked Phil DiSarro for the original design, alongside the CIP reviewers and editors. Credit also goes to Michele Nuzzi from Harmonic Labs [, who was among the first to explore programmable token implementations on Cardano. Matteo Coppola]( Matteo on X: "After many years of work, CIP113 has been officially merged to the main branch of Cardano CIPs. This means the official standard for programmable tokens on Cardano, including securities, is out. Many great minds have contributed to the standard, but in particular @CryptoJoe101 has … / X ) of FluidTokens (also an active collaborator) and Danny Ribar of Project Catalyst also highlighted the years of work behind the standard, with Danny pointing to the next challenge: adoption. Adam Dean described the merge as another step toward Active status. For a closer technical look, the Cardano Developer Office Hour with Giovanni covers CIP-113 and its KYC substandard. Read the CIP and its discussion on GitHub. Cardano Node Update + Reminder for This Week’s SPO Call Intersect has released Cardano Node version 11.1.3, a small but important technical update for SPOs and node operators. The release fixes an issue with IPv4 address decoding introduced in 11.1.2, following an issue identified on the Preprod testnet. Intersect recommends that SPOs run version 11.1.2 at minimum, while anyone still running an older version should move directly to 11.1.3. And the good news… no ledger replay is required! The update is mainly a corrective release rather than a feature upgrade. This one keeps the focus on maintaining network stability and consistent node operation. Full release details and changelog . Oh, and one more thing: don’t forget to join this week’s SPO Call on Thursday, October 1st, at 15:00 UTC. The call will cover the latest core node updates, Leios and the Musashi testnet, node diversity with Blink Labs and Dingo, and the latest developments around Mithril. As always, all SPOs are encouraged to come on stage and join the discussion, so bring your questions. Add the call to your calendar Cardano at TOKEN2049: Singapore, Here We Come - 1 Week To Go TOKEN2049 Singapore is just over a week away, and the Cardano Foundation will be there as a Platinum Sponsor , bringing a 108m² Cardano booth to Marina Bay Sands on October 7–8. Catch the full announcement here. The Cardano Booth will feature 20 selected Cardano ecosystem projects, giving attendees the chance to meet and interact directly with the teams building across the ecosystem. There will also be a podcast corner, builder presentations, and a dedicated program around node diversity, including the Node Diversity Celebration Day on October 6. Curious about all this? Well… check out the Cardano TOKEN2049 website for the full overview, including the list of projects representing the ecosystem. The TOKEN2049 Origins Hackathon, side events ( such as the Rooftop UTXO Pitch Night with Draper Dragon ) and other activities will add to a busy week. Intersect has also confirmed its participation at the Cardano booth, while Midnight will be present at TOKEN2049 with its own program. Intersect update Midnight event schedule . And if you missed last week’s Cardano Foundation AMA on X , it’s worth catching up on before the event. Developer Spotlight: ODATANO In the latest Developer Spotlight, Maximilian Weber , creator of ODATANO, shares how his background in SAP development and interest in decentralised systems led him to explore Cardano’s potential in the enterprise space. The interview looks at how ODATANO uses OData, a standard already familiar to SAP developers, to make it easier for enterprise systems to interact with Cardano without requiring developers to navigate the full complexity of blockchain integration. Max also takes us through projects such as TRACE and QUANTIX, showing how Cardano can be applied to areas including supply chains, procurement and financial data. He also shares his perspective on where Cardano is well suited for enterprise adoption, what still needs to improve, and what it could take to move blockchain from a developer’s laptop into real-world business systems. Read the full Developer Spotlight Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates Another batch of CIPs just landed, and this one has a clear theme: making Cardano more resilient, more observable, and easier to trust. Robert Phair ’s latest snapshot brings six new proposals to the table, from a messaging framework built for “rescue” scenarios to tools that shed light on what our nodes are really doing. And a long-awaited heavy hitter has finally crossed the finish line. New Proposals Related CIP & CPS for a trusted messaging framework for Cardano, with a range of Cardano-specific and Internet-wide options; including off-chain operation for use in “rescue” scenarios: CPS-0038 candidate: Trustworthy Off-chain Message Dissemination CIP-0201 candidate: Decentralised Pub/Sub Message Dissemination Two different proposals for diagnostics through Cardano’s multi-node diversification: CIP-0202 candidate: Node Observability Snapshot Protocol - universal metrics for each node’s performance CIP-0203 candidate: Block Producer Identifier Registry - for including the node type in each produced block And a couple more worth a look: CIP-0204 candidate: Holder Answers on Governance Actions CIP-0205 candidate: Remove scope check in Plutus Core Active Review CIP-0200 candidate: Transaction Urgency Signalling On Linear Leios - experts are weighing in on the tension between ideal performance and cost efficiency versus real-world economics and business requirements Completed CIP-0113 | Programmable token-like assets - it made it across the line! Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates Cardanians Newsletter #142 landed September 28 covering several great updates from the ecosystem. Charles Hoskinson, for example, framed Midnight’s private smart contracts and private asset transfers as a structural step forward from existing privacy chains. Further more, the newsletter also highlights JamOnBread’s NFT marketplace relaunched on Cardano. And an AlphaGrowth DeFi protocol audit flagged eight gaps in the current Cardano DeFi setup, which is a must-read if you build or use DeFi on-chain. Full thread on their X profile. Catch the full thread here . Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #145 Lucas Macchiavelli is back with Issue #145 , out September 28. It covers the Barça Fan Lab launch, the Fireblocks Native Token custody news, and the Lace 2.3 wallet update that redesigns stake pool and DRep discovery. This and much more in the latest Cardsano Newsletter. Check the full issue on his site: Weekly Cardano Digest #145 . Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators Cardano’s got no shortage of people documenting it, explaining it, and building on it out in the open, and this week we’re giving them their flowers. Below is a mix of voices: creators breaking down technical upgrades and staking basics for newcomers, and builders giving firsthand updates on what they’re shipping. A few Content Creator Spotlights from across the ecosystem:: Cardano Ambassador, Peter Bui recently posted a video titled; “Cardano and Midnight Are Getting More Usable,”. This roughly thirty-five-minute ecosystem recap pulls together the week’s biggest developments: from Fireblocks integration, to Barça Fan Lab using Cardano, to the Catalyst 2026 Pilot update, and Cardano Venture Hub updates. Definitely a great pick if you’d rather sit down with one coherent story. Watch here . Community member Sadık Emre ALKAN shared a thoughtful educational (back to basics) explainer on Cardano’s research-first methodology, contrasting it with ‘build-first chains’ and extending his argument to why Midnight’s zero-knowledge design follows the same commitments. It’s a longer read, but a rewarding one for anyone interested in the protocol’s underlying design philosophy. Read here the X post. Community Learning & Developer Engagement The September 28 issued Developers Office Hour featured Dominic Wallis (Senior Software Engineer at Cardano Foundation) presenting Subbit.xyz , a lightweight L2 payment channel protocol for trustless subscriptions and micropayments. The session is a practical complement to the broader x402 agentic payments story that has been developing across the Cardano ecosystem for some time now already. If you’re interested in learning more about this , the confirmed Hydra Technical Workshop on October 2 at 14:00 UTC will cover the Hydra state channel framework, practical application use cases, technical setup steps, and a live Q&A with the Hydra team. So developers curious about high-throughput Layer 2 applications on Cardano should mark the date. Also on September 28, the Roundtable Talk: Smart Contract Security - Why One Check Is No Longer Enough brought together experienced security professionals to explore how the rapidly evolving AI landscape is changing smart contract security. The discussion looked at how AI models can now analyse code, identify vulnerabilities, and generate exploit code in minutes, raising new questions around continuous monitoring, the role of traditional audits, and trust across the ecosystem. The panel also discussed how auditing firms are adapting their business models and what practical steps DApp developers can take to strengthen security and protect users. The session featured Alexander Vershilov, Senior Security Researcher at Tweag ; Santi Carmuega , CEO of TxPipe ; Philip DiSarro , CEO of Anastasia Labs; Samuel Leathers , Security Counsel at Intersect MBO , and Benjamin Hart, CTO & Technical Architect at MLabs . Rewatch the episode here. Updates from the Cardano Foundation The Cardano Foundation’s been busy, as always, with updates spanning education, real-world adoption, the x402 agentic economy, and governance. Starting with education: on September 28, the Foundation announced a multi-year partnership with the Venture Accelerator at UCLA Anderson School of Management . The collaboration includes five sponsored fellowships for early-stage companies in the UCLA Accelerate programme, an interactive blockchain and AI masterclass on October 19 titled “Cardano for the Real World,” Cardano Academy content being integrated into UCLA Anderson’s blockchain coursework from 2027, and sponsorship of the 2027 UCLA Draper Innovation Showcase. Full partnership details at crypto.news . On the adoption front, FC Barcelona formally launched the Barça Fan Lab on Cardano on September 25 . Funded through Catalyst Fund 13 and built in collaboration with Andamio, the platform connects fans’ existing BarçaID digital identity with a Cardano Web3 wallet, opening the door to verifiable credentials, educational badges, access tokens, and collectibles without requiring participants to have advanced blockchain knowledge. Then there’s the x402 push. The Foundation confirmed Cardano is now live in the official x402 SDK , with CF engineers contributing client, server, and facilitator components that enable ada-denominated API payments for AI agents and applications. That puts Cardano into the broader x402 initiative championed by Coinbase, which is focused on machine-to-machine payments over standard HTTP. And September 23 marked nine years of Cardano. The Foundation shared the birthday stats : 38.89 billion ada circulating, 21.29 billion ada staked across 2,672 active stake pools, 328 active DReps, and 158 governance actions recorded since the start of the Voltaire era. Meanwhile, the UNDP SDG Blockchain Accelerator application window is entering its final week, with UN teams invited to submit real-world challenges that blockchain technology could potentially help address. And on September 22, the CF-hosted X Space “What’s next for Cardano?” brought together CEO Frederik Gregaard, contributors from the Amaru alternative node team, and the community for a discussion covering the Catalyst 2026 Pilot design and plans for community events in 2027. Update from Intersect MBO Intersect announced the results of its 2026 Board elections on September 28, with Adam Rusch and Kavinda Kariyapperuma elected from a field of 11 candidates. A total of 139 Intersect members cast their votes. Intersect also thanked the nine candidates who were not elected and encouraged them to remain involved through its committees and working groups. The latest Intersect Weekly Update #130 , published on September 26, also highlighted several governance and technical developments. The Civics Committee completed the refresh of its knowledge base, restructuring governance documentation and adding dedicated pages covering the Constitutional Committee reduction to five seats, the global Constitution consultation, and the 2026 CC election. On the technical side, the Node Development Roadmap indicates that Node 11.2 is expected to introduce the first Dijkstra-era features, including Plutus V4. Meanwhile, the Parameter Committee is assessing around 150 combined Dijkstra and Peras guardrails. Read the full update on the Intersect news page . Several on-chain governance actions are also approaching their October 11 expiry, including the OpenZeppelin Stack treasury withdrawal, a proposal to reduce minPoolCost to 75 ADA, and a stake pool target k-parameter poll. DReps and SPOs are encouraged to review the proposals and cast their votes before the deadline. If you’re interested in rewatching the deep-dive Governance Hour sessions with Nicolas Cerny , you can find them here: OpenZeppelin and Reduce minPoolCost to 75 ADA ( Cerkoryn ). The Constitutional Amendment Portal (CAP) remains open for community consultation, with seven proposals currently under review. CAP-3, the Net Change Limit Strategic Spending Plan, has received the most engagement so far, with 18 community comments. items.description: ** ** Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: TOKEN2049 Origins Hackathon: Build AI agent payment solutions on Cardano using x402, 36 hours, $27,500 in prizes. Applications close September 18. Constitutional Amendment Portal: Seven proposals in consultation, review call with proposers and community on September 17. Intersect Board Elections 2026: Eleven candidates, two seats, voting open until September 25, results September 28. SDG Blockchain Accelerator: Cardano track offers equity-free funding and mentorship for up to four teams. Applications close September 30. Ambassador Stories: Meet Baudouin, connecting Francophone African communities with Cardano through education and governance. CIP Updates: Five new proposals, from Plutus cryptography to minUTxO friction, plus CIP-113 and CIP-192 in active review. Ecosystem & Creator Highlights: Cardanians covers PRIME, SundaeSwap v4, and Midnight City; creators dig into blocks, x402, and staking. Community Learning: RealFi, a Leios demo hitting ~1,000 TPS, and Governance Hour #10 on the OpenZeppelin Stack proposal (open until October 11). CF & Intersect Updates: August highlights, Blockforce’s supply chain rollout, TOKEN2049 plans, plus the new Constitutional Committee and Dijkstra prep. All this and more in today’s Digest. DEADLINE EXTENDED: Token2049 Origins Hackathon, 6-8 October 2026 Heads up, builders: applications for the Cardano track at the TOKEN2049 Origins Hackathon just got extended to September 18, so you’ve got a few extra days to throw your hat in. The challenge is a fun one: figure out how AI agents and autonomous apps can transact on Cardano using x402, the open payment standard built for programmatic, machine-to-machine payments. You’ll get 36 hours, October 6–7 in Singapore, to go from idea to working product and demo it live on the main stage. There are 200 free spots up for grabs and $27,500 in prizes split across three winners, basically a playground for experimenting with agent-to-agent payments, autonomous services, and whatever the agentic economy turns into next. Want in? Applications close September 18. Full announcement and details here CAP Review Call: Go Through The Open Amendment Proposals with Proposers and Reviewers The Constitutional Amendment Portal has been live for six weeks. In that time, five constitutional amendment proposals (CAPs) and two constitutional issue statements (CIS) have been submitted. All seven are in consultation right now. Tomorrow, 17 September 2026, Intersect hosts a CAP Review call: a focused session to go through the open proposals, to facilitate discussions between the proposers, editors and the community. Hear directly from the proposers and the reviewers, and bring your own questions. Thursday 17 September, 09:00 to 10:00 CEST Register: CAP Review · Luma Browse the proposals: Constitutional Amendment Portal — Cardano Constitution Intersect Board Elections 2026: Voting Open Until September 25, 2026 Voting in the Intersect Board Elections 2026 kicked off September 14, with eleven candidates duking it out for two community-elected Board seats, each carrying a two-year term. On the ballot: Adam Rusch , Alexa K. , Anuj Chaudhary , Christian Taylor , Eric Helms, I an McCullough , Jose Miguel De Gamboa , Kavinda Kariyapperuma , Ken Erik Ølmheim , Nana Safo , and Ridwan Itopa Musa . Polls stay open through September 25, with results dropping September 28. Eligible voters need 180 days of active Intersect standing and completed KYC. Two candidate forums, September 15 and 22, give the community a shot to grill each contender before ballots close. Full details are right here . Want to hear straight from the candidates before locking in your vote? Intersect recently hosted a live Q&A session where candidates introduced themselves and fielded questions on their vision for the seat, worth a listen if you’re still deciding. Call To Action: Cardano Track Open for the SDG Blockchain Accelerator Cohort 3 Got a solution that could actually move the needle on real-world problems? Applications are open for Cohort 3 of the SDG Blockchain Accelerator, a joint effort between the Cardano Foundation , UNDP AltFinLab , and Chain for Good . This round, the Foundation’s putting serious weight behind a dedicated Cardano track. Up to four teams get selected for equity-free funding, hands-on technical mentorship, and direct integration support, tackling real challenges straight from UN country offices. Think digital identity, payments, supply chain traceability, and transparent data systems, the kind of work that actually ships. The acceleration runs four months, October 2026 through February 2027, with a real shot at public-sector deployment on the other end. Applications close September 30 For more details check out the UNDP post here. Ambassador Stories, with Baudouin Kakule Muvunga Meet Baudouin, one of the newest faces in the Cardano Ambassador Program. Based in the Democratic Republic of Congo, his journey into blockchain kicked off as a student after stumbling into a local Cardano community event. What hooked him wasn’t the price charts, it was the idea that blockchain could go way beyond crypto and actually tackle real-world problems. With a background in rural development, humanitarian work, human rights, and community building, Baudouin saw an obvious overlap between Cardano and the work he was already doing. Today he leads the Nyiragongo Cardano Hub, connecting Francophone African communities with Web3 through education, financial inclusion, digital identity, and decentralized governance. As an Ambassador, he’s all about building bridges, linking the global Cardano ecosystem with communities across the DRC and Africa. That means meetups, workshops, governance discussions, and training, all aimed at turning local communities into active participants instead of passive users. His vision going forward: Cardano driving real, tangible impact across Africa. Catch Baudouin’s full story here . Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates Fresh batch of CIPs recently dropped, and this one’s stacked. Robert Phair ’s latest snapshot brings five new proposals to the table, from Plutus-level cryptography to network signalling, plus a couple of heavy hitters closing in on the finish line. And there’s a new face joining the Editor Crew. Say hi to Sebastian Nagel (GitHub: @ch1bo ), the latest addition to the CIP Editors team. Long-time key developer, long-time community fixture, now officially part of the review squad. New Proposals CIP-0199 candidate: Poseidon Permutation Built-in for Plutus CIP-0200 candidate: Urgency Signalling in Linear Leios CPS-0035 candidate: Digital Product Passports CPS-0036 candidate: Voluntary Block Producer Software Signalling CPS-0037 candidate: Application and transaction friction in minUTxO implementation Active Review CIP-0113 candidate: Programmable token-like assets - final call for review before merge! CIP-0192 candidate: Transaction Fee-Change Field - discussion of effects on Tx determinism Completed CPS-0031: Prioritising Urgent Transactions Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates Cardanians Newsletter #140 dropped September 14 with a headline that’s been a long time coming: Cardano PRIME is officially open for project submissions, the ecosystem’s flagship on-chain governance-funded program for scaling grants and innovation. Also on deck: SundaeSwap v4 targeting mainnet October 1 with concentrated liquidity, modular pools, and automated routing, plus Midnight City hitting 600 active agents on Midnight’s privacy layer, an early but real signal of protocol activity. Catch the full thread here . Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #141 Issue #143 of the Cardano Newsletter is out! This time Lucas Macchiavelli breaks down the x402 merge and what it means for Cardano’s spot in the agentic payment economy, plus a look at SundaeSwap v4’s October 1 launch window. As always, tight, and reliably useful. Check the full issue on his site: Weekly Cardano Digest #143 Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators Cardano’s got no shortage of people documenting it, explaining it, and building on it out in the open, and this week we’re giving them their flowers. Below is a mix of voices: creators breaking down technical upgrades and staking basics for newcomers, and builders giving firsthand updates on what they’re shipping. A few Content Creator Spotlights from across the ecosystem:: MB (@Mb_you_know) kept the streak alive with Day 21 of their daily Cardano thread series, “What Is Inside a Cardano Block?” He walks through the basics: transactions, the header that ties a block to the one before it, the cryptographic link that makes the chain a chain, and the producer data used to verify who signed it. For this and more, see Day 21 here. The Crypto Dossier channel dropped a September 13 video on the x402 Cardano integration, now past 10,000 views. It covers Cardano moving from spec-only to a working implementation in the official x402 repo, so apps and AI agents can pay per request, plus extras like Masumi’s optional trust layer. For this and more, watch the video here . Linda (@Cryptofly777) posted her weekly Cardano update on September 14, calling it a week of adoption. She hits ada and stablecoins in WhatsApp, stablecoins meeting the real economy, and AlphaGrowth’s push to bring in EVM users and make capital more efficient. For this and more, watch the update here . **Community Learning & Developer Engagement ** This week’s Cardano Seminar spotlighted RealFi, with CEO John O’Connor breaking down how the project turns idle on-chain dollars into yield backed by real-world credit, complete with a three-token setup, built-in risk protections, and a look at what’s next on the road to mainnet. Watch it here . Separately, Carlos Lopez de Lara sat down with Ouroboros Leios architect Sebastian Nagel for a live lab demo, pushing a local Leios cluster to 250 TxkB/s (about 1,000 TPS), well past mainnet’s current ceiling. The next challenge: making those numbers hold up on the real internet. Missed it? Watch it here ! Cardano Governance Hours #10 took a closer look at the live treasury withdrawal asking for 11,787,063 ada to fund the OpenZeppelin Stack, administered by Intersect. Arturo Beccar-Varela of OpenZeppelin walks through the 12-month plan: audited open-source libraries plus three reference implementations covering liquid staking, self-repaying loans, and a tokenized money market fund, with developer enablement included. Catch the full episode here . Updates from the Cardano Foundation The Cardano Foundation ’s been busy, dropping updates that span everything from enterprise wins and institutional outreach to global events, education, and governance. As per the Cardano Foundation ’s August 2026 ecosystem update, published September 8, it was a stacked month: the IBC bridge audit cleared (Cosmos interoperability, officially unlocked), 160 Olympic Committee staff went through CF’s blockchain education program, and Reeve 1.7 shipped, the Foundation’s on-chain financial data toolset. Full breakdown here . Biggest flex of the update, according to the Foundation, goes to Blockforce , whose supply chain platform went live on Cardano August 31 and got its own formal Cardano Foundation case study on September 7. Per that case study, the numbers are wild: 500,000+ supply chain records already anchored on-chain. The setup runs a dual-ledger architecture, sensitive commercial data stays private on a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric network, while cryptographic fingerprints get anchored publicly on Cardano. Using a batching tool called uVerify, they’re grouping up to 44 certificates per transaction, which the Foundation says cuts cost per record by 92%. The first big deployment is Azzas 2154, Latin America’s largest fashion group, tracking its leather supply chain across 6,200+ suppliers to stay compliant with the EU’s deforestation rules, with 95,000+ invoices already processed and a contracted target of 6.5 million records by 2030. Also on September 8 , the Foundation announced that for TOKEN2049 they’re co-hosting the Rooftop UTXO Pitch Night , with Draper Dragon putting up to $500,000 on the table for selected teams. There’s also a TOKEN2049 Origins Hackathon track dedicated to the Cardano x402 agentic economy, $27,500 in prizes on the line. Finally… a little history lesson on where the “Cardano” name actually comes from, Renaissance mathematician Gerolamo Cardano (1501–1576). Source: Cardano Foundation on X: "Ever wondered why it's called Cardano? Cardano is named after Gerolamo Cardano (1501–1576), the Italian mathematician & polymath who pioneered early cryptography. A fitting tribute for a blockchain built on peer-reviewed research, math, and science." / X Update from Intersect MBO From Intersect’s Weekly Update #128 : the newly elected Constitutional Committee officially took its seat in Epoch 654 following the ratified Update Constitutional Committee 2026 action, and GovTool’s active maintenance has moved to Sireto, led by original builder Sandip Pandey, who’s committed to keeping it open source and easy to self-host. Full update here. There are also three governance actions still live with deadlines approaching rapidly: the Governance Incentives Framework 2026 (expires September 16, sitting at 1.62% DRep support), the Ikigai Info deposit reimbursement (expires September 16, at 58.26% DRep support), and the OpenZeppelin Stack treasury withdrawal of 11,787,063 ada (expires October 11, currently at 0.02% DRep support). Get your votes in before those windows close. And finally, ChangWatch has officially rebranded as GovScope, with the transition kicking off September 13. As the ecosystem prepares for its next major milestone, the Dijkstra era, node versions 11.1.1 and 11.2 are already paving the way for advanced protocol capabilities, node diversity, and dedicated testnet environments. Lots of great updates, but if you’d like to follow through on the Upgrade Bulletin for the full story, read here . items.title: Cardano Global Events 2027: The Catch-up
items.description: Every new event at the Cardano Foundation goes through five key stages: research, conceptualization, planning, execution and reporting. Working within the Cardano Ecosystem we then build in important additional layers to this cyclical process in order to ensure our work delivers for the wider Cardano ecosystem and community. Why the first Unified Global Events Marketing Strategy worked The 2025/26 Unified Global Events Marketing Strategy was a major success for the Cardano ecosystem. Together with EMURGO and Rare Network, the Cardano Foundation executed a 12-month, Treasury funded events series spanning four continents. From Blockchain Rio in August 2025 to WebX Asia in Tokyo in July 2026, the series included 20 unique event experiences including booths, sponsorships and side events, each providing a high profile platform for 79 Cardano projects. Performance exceeded every metric detailed in the original Treasury proposal: Booth Activations reaching 8,191 total contacts Developer engagement securing 1,169 participating developers Institutional Partnerships : meaningful engagement with key 50 government and regulatory authorities, 143 corporate entities, and 26 academic institutions. Thought Leadership : 27 keynote addresses and panel appearances Media Coverage: 147 published articles and broadcast interviews Ecosystem Growth : the booth facilitated ecosystem growth, generating: 1,045 Cardano wallet sign-ups (reaching 201% of the target), 1,244 Cardano Academy subscribers (222% of the goal), 102 hackathon registrations 56 expert-led workshops and builder presentations hosted at the booths Overall visibility, digital engagement and branding recognition increased significantly, with social media channels across all three participating organizations experiencing substantial growth throughout the campaign. In terms of our technical audience, we saw a greater developer attendance in: Rio de Janeiro for Latin America, Nairobi for Africa, Paris for Europe (54% of booth attendance being developers), Hong Kong for Asia. The Cardano Developer Portal provided them with a perfect entry point to Cardano. It furnishes seasoned professionals with access to Java, TypeScript, Python and Rust libraries, and takes newcomers from their first transaction to the full deployment of DApps. A newly created subscription to updates on technical jobs, hackathons, or grants also increases the chances of new developers staying connected to Cardano. The reported Impact: See the final KPI results per event here. The clock is ticking and the potential is real We are now at the end of one cycle and the beginning of another. As we approach TOKEN2049, we are at once excited to host the biggest Cardano event ever in Asia-Pacific while looking ahead to what’s next. We are already planning how to build on the success of this campaign with another even stronger series in 2027. This means starting now. If this strategy is approved by the community, we would kick off this series in February 2027 with the Africa Tech Summit. Large events require extensive financial and logistical advance planning and so, with the clock ticking and deadlines looming, we want to share some more information on what this could look like. To ensure we match and, where possible, surpass the high bar we set with the first series, we’re proposing to run this next series through the calendar year January to December 2027. Within this 12 month timeline we would target 11 world class conferences, developing activations to amplify the Cardano brand across Europe, Asia, Australia, Africa, Latin America, and the USA. Each event and location are chosen to ensure maximum leverage for the team to host a cohesive, unified Cardano booth and to provide selected builders (supported via online application) with high profile opportunities to showcase their solutions, and accelerate business growth while onsite. Complementing this, each event would incorporate strategically unified Cardano branding, speaking opportunities where possible, and media outreach campaigns. This is our 2027 Unified Marketing Events wishlist: The 2027 strategy rests on four pillars: 1. Builders as the core ecosystem participants. This strategy exists first and foremost to give Cardano’s builders and ecosystem projects a platform at major global conferences. 2. Centralized accountability, local delivery. The Cardano Foundation holds overall responsibility for the strategy’s delivery and outcomes, ensuring accountability and consistency in Treasury reporting and branding across all activations with the support of local ecosystem partners and ambassadors. 3. Alignment with the Cardano 2030 strategic vision. This proposal directly supports Pillar 4: Community & Ecosystem Growth of the Cardano 2030 Strategy , which calls for global engagement through a market-centric approach, targeting high-impact regions, (naming LATAM, Africa, and East Asia) with localized partnerships and communication. 4. A leaner, more predictable calendar year. Each activation will concentrate resources to achieve, higher-impact moments, on a calendar which has a clearly predictable annual cadence that can be repeated going forward. The Budget We are budgeting for all events listed to fall within a 5M USD budget to cover the external costs of the execution, the Cardano Foundation will not generate a profit from this proposal. The full budget per event, including the split between booth costs and ecosystem travel support, updated KPI targets, Treasury withdrawal, budget dependencies and reporting mechanics will be set out in the proposal itself. So What Next? In order to move forward we need the support of the community. Next steps would involve finalizing and presenting a draft for a full proposal and beginning the Treasury withdrawal process, subject to NCL availability and community feedback. We’ll share further information for the 2027 events plan in due course. We look forward to keeping the positive momentum going throughout the remainder of 2026 and 2027. We welcome all comments and thoughts - please share them in this forum. We will also host an AMA on X to further engage on this topic in the coming weeks. items.title: Digest September 02, 2026: Intersect Board Elections 2026 | Constitutional Amendment Portal | Stake Pool Operator Scripts Update | Daedalus 11.3.0 | Ambassador Stories: Ayomide Osemene
items.description: ! Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: Intersect Board Elections 2026: Applications are now open for two elected Intersect Board seats, with voting scheduled for September 14–25 and results expected on September 28. Constitutional Amendment Portal: The new alpha portal gives ada holders a more accessible way to propose, discuss, and follow potential amendments to the Cardano Constitution. Stake Pool Operator Scripts Update: New SPO scripts add support for upcoming LedgerApp v8, HW-CLI 1.20, and Cardano-Signer v1.35, alongside improved governance voting and Ledger operations. Daedalus 11.3.0: The latest Daedalus release introduces a DRep Directory, improved governance features, wallet support, reliability updates, and the new Ariadne support portal. Ambassador Stories – Ayomide Osemene: New Ambassador Ayomide shares how Project Catalyst sparked his journey into Cardano and his passion for education, collaboration, and helping others engage with the ecosystem. Cardano Improvement Proposals: This week’s CIP snapshot covers a new proposal for a Nested Transactions service layer, the ongoing CIP-113 audit, and three proposals that have completed the process. Ecosystem & Creator Highlights: Cardanians highlights progress with Ouroboros Leios and growing ecosystem activity, while creators cover Hydra, node infrastructure, and Cardano fundamentals. All this and more in today’s Digest. Intersect Board Elections 2026: Applications Now Opened Intersect has opened applications for its 2026 Board Elections, with two member-elected Board seats available as the terms of Adam Rusch and Kavinda Kariyapperuma come to an end. As per Intersect’s comms, applications opened on August 31 at 12:00 UTC and will remain open until September 11 at 12:00 UTC. Voting is scheduled for September 14–25, with the results expected on September 28. To be eligible for election, candidates must have been an Intersect member for at least 180 days, be in good standing, have completed identity verification, and have previously served at least one term on an Intersect Committee or the Board. But what does the Board actually do? Well… The Board plays an important role in setting Intersect MBO’s strategic priorities and overseeing the organisation, making the election an opportunity for eligible members to have a direct say in its future direction. Intersect is encouraging eligible members considering a candidacy to review the requirements and prepare their applications before the deadline. Sounds interesting? Check out the full story here. The Constitutional Amendment Portal: A Real Process For Changing The Constitution Any ada holder can propose an amendment to the Cardano Constitution. In practice, few do. You need 100,000 ada for the governance action deposit and you need to submit a valid governance action on-chain. Possible, but far from accessible for the average ada holder. That is why the Intersect Civics Committee stood up the Constitutional Amendment Process Working Group in September 2025. The group pulled in IOG, the Cardano Foundation, Intersect, the Constitutional Committee, DReps, SPOs, constitutional delegates and community members. It defined the requirements such a process and tool would have to meet, then built it. Since early August 2026, the Constitutional Amendment Portal (CAP) has been live in alpha. Connect a CIP-30 wallet, pick a username, and you are in. No email, no password. You can propose an amendment by highlighting the passage you want to change and explaining why, raise a Constitutional Issue Statement if you have spotted a problem but not the fix, or comment on what others have put forward and follow it through consultation, ready and done. It is an alpha, released early on purpose, which means the feedback you give now shapes what it becomes. Try it: https://cap.intersectmbo.org Stake Pool Operator Scripts Update Martin Lang ( ATADA Pool ) has released a new update for the StakePool Operator Scripts (SPOS), bringing support for upcoming LedgerApp v8, HW-CLI 1.20, and Cardano-Signer v1.35. Currently available in the testnet directory on GitHub ahead of the official LedgerApp v8 release, key updates include: Batch Governance Voting: Added “unrestricted” signing mode allowing Ledger hardware wallets to sign votes on multiple governance actions simultaneously using a DRep key (24b). DRep Key & Payment Flexibility: Enhanced flexibility for DRep registration and retirement operations (21b, 21d), allowing CLI-wallet funding for Ledger DRep operations and Ledger payment for CLI-Key DRep actions. Direct Pool Operations: SPOs can now register or update a stake pool directly using the pool key and payment key stored on a Ledger hardware wallet (05c). Detailed HW Error Reporting: Enhanced, detailed error messaging across 15+ transaction and certification scripts (including rewards claims, asset transfers, delegation, and minting/burning). SPOs preparing for Ledger v8 testing can access the updated scripts directly in the project’s GitHub repository . Daedalus 11.3.0 Released Daedalus 11.3.0 was announced on September 1, bringing new governance tools, improved wallet support and reliability updates. According to SE7EN Labs , the release adds a DRep Directory to the Governance Center, allowing users to search, sort and filter DReps, review their details and delegate voting power directly from Daedalus. Users can also delegate to Abstain or No Confidence. It also introduces Ariadne, SE7EN Labs’ new Daedalus support portal, while explorer links have been updated and outdated endpoints removed. Compatibility for some Byron-era wallets has been improved, addressing an issue affecting normal wallet use. Daedalus 11.3.0 also adds a new process watchdog to improve process restarts, log rotation and shutdowns. Mithril fast-forward support and a Linux GPU recovery option complete the update. For the full run down, check out the X thread announcement here Ambassador Stories, with Ayomide Osemene Meet Ayomide , one of the newest Ambassadors to join the Cardano Ambassador Program. Her journey into Cardano began at university through Project Catalyst, which sparked her curiosity and led her to explore the ecosystem, connect with the community, and keep learning. With a background in mathematics, product management, education, and event coordination, Ayomide is passionate about helping others understand complex ideas and creating opportunities for people to learn and participate. Cardano also introduced her to decentralization and, along the way, showed her that her voice and perspective could contribute to the conversation. As an Ambassador, Ayomide wants to use her skills, voice, and passion to help more people understand and engage with Cardano. For her, that means education, collaboration, and consistent community participation, while also knowing when to point people toward the right resources and experienced voices. Looking ahead, Ayomide’s vision is simple: mass adoption! So… want to discover how a university student who first encountered Cardano through Project Catalyst became an Ambassador helping others find their way into the ecosystem? Catch Ayomide’s full story here. Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates This week’s Cardano Improvement Proposal (CIP) snapshot from Robert Phair offers another look at the ideas and technical work moving through Cardano’s open proposal process. There’s a new proposal exploring a service layer for Nested Transactions, an ongoing audit of CIP-113, and three proposals that have now completed the process. It’s a good illustration of how ideas can enter the discussion, go through community review and technical scrutiny, and ultimately either move toward adoption or become useful reference points for future development. New Proposals CIP-0198 candidate: Nested Transactions - Service Layer - an off-chain mechanism to publicise and assemble intent-based transactions (such as “babel fees” in token swaps): compatible with Nested Transactions ( CIP-0118 ) in the Cardano Ledger, using network protocols such as the node’s Decentralized Message Queue ( CIP-0137 ) Active Review CIP-0113 candidate: Programmable token-like assets - audit in progress (no major findings) Completed CIP-0178: Merkle Root of Transactions in Block Header CIP-0188: Token-Owned Addresses CPS-0030: Quantum-secure settlement layer Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates On 31 August, 2026, Cardanians (CRDN) published Newsletter #138 , covering what they described as one of Cardano’s busiest weeks in months. The issue puts Ouroboros Leios front and center, highlighting the 500% throughput increase achieved during the Musashi Dojo Earth phase testnet, with four more phases to go and a year-end hard fork now broadly expected. The newsletter also looks at Cardano’s growing activity, with monthly active addresses rising 38% to 266,500 according to TokenTerminal, alongside the first Japanese exchange listing for midnight-3. For the full breakdown, check out the Cardanians X thread . Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #141 Lucas is back with another Weekly Cardano Newsletter, this time with #141 . This week’s edition shines a spotlight on three standout developments across the ecosystem. First up, Cardano Lightning has entered pre-production with a state channel architecture built on a fork of the Lightning Development Kit, marking an important step forward for Cardano’s payment infrastructure. Second, Plutus 1.68.0.0 shipped during the week, bringing Plutus V4 ledger API types ahead of the Dijkstra hard fork, along with improvements to Data constructor casing and new builtins aimed at improving script performance. And third, Midnight City has progressed to a visualization environment designed to scale to millions of participants, moving beyond earlier demo-scale deployments. Check out the full issue at Lucas’s newsletter site: Weekly Cardano Digest #141 Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators Cardano’s ecosystem is full of people documenting it, explaining it, and building on it in public, and we want to take a moment to recognize their contributions. This week’s roundup brings together a mix of voices: creators breaking down technical upgrades and staking fundamentals for newcomers, and builders sharing firsthand updates on what they’re shipping. Here are a few Content Creators Spotlight from across the ecosystem: Cheeky Crypto Unfiltered recently dropped a set of two videos diving into several of Cardano’s infrastructure upgrades. The first, titled “ Cardano Hydra Just Got a Lot Faster ”, covers how Hydra switched the way it stores data behind the scenes (from JSON to a more compact format called CBOR). According to the video, this shrank a 3-node test database by more than half, from 27.4MB down to 10.5MB, with the switch happening automatically. He also notes that data sent between nodes is now smaller too, and everything reads and writes up to 21× faster. The second video, titled “ Cardano’s Node Problem Is Quietly Being Rebuilt ,” zooms out from that Layer 2 upgrade to look at the core infrastructure. As he lays out, several pieces are in motion: a new version called Mithril 2630, “certified snapshots” that let new nodes verify they’re syncing the right data, an early-stage messaging system (DMQ), support for multiple independent verifiers instead of relying on one, and an experimental way to store node data using IPFS (a decentralized file-sharing system). He’s careful to note it’s all still in testing, not finished, but the way nodes get up and running is being reworked from the ground up. For a while now, MB ( @Mb_you_know ) has been running a daily ELI5 explainer series breaking down Cardano and blockchain concepts one topic at a time. His latest post, Day 16, covers what happens at the end of a Cardano epoch, but the series builds from the ground up, touching on how to choose a good stake pool, what delegation actually means, how staking rewards are calculated along the way, and much more. You can follow the thread from the start by working back through his previous posts: See Day 16 here Community Learning & Developer Engagement During a recent Developer Office Hours, Zack “Cash” Soesbee (CEO) and Patrick “PB” (COO) of Anvil Development Agency gave a behind-the-scenes look at what the team has built on Cardano, from tools like Weld, the Anvil API, and their WayUp marketplace to newer efforts like Hodei, a seedless wallet, and Sellout.io , a ticketing platform, and more. According to Cash, their focus now is real-world adoption: building ordinary software for businesses first, earning their trust, then introducing blockchain later, as they did with Blom, an industrial paint company whose quoting process they cut from two hours to thirty minutes: Watch it here From one Cardano-native team to another, a separate Developer Office Hours session brought on Albina , Sandro , and Patrick from Masumi for an update on the Masumi ecosystem. They cover recent developments across the network and what’s coming next, touching on Masumi, Sokosumi, highlighted agents, the Dev Hub, and the business vision behind collaborations and x402. The session also digs into Masumi Smart Contract V2, Hydra integration, Veridian Agent Certification, and the latest roadmap: Watch it here . Updates from the Cardano Foundation The Cardano Foundation has shared several recent updates, highlighting ecosystem progress across enterprise adoption, institutional outreach, global events, education, and governance. On August 31, Blockforce’s traceability platform officially went live on Cardano as its public proof layer , with over 500,000 supply chain records already anchored on-chain. Here’s how it works: the commercial data stays private on a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric layer, while cryptographic proofs get published to Cardano so auditors, regulators, and end customers can independently verify record integrity without ever touching the underlying data. Joint engineering work between Blockforce and the Foundation managed to cut the per-record cost by 92%, and signed contracts now cover 6.5 million certification records through 2030 across fashion, automotive, agribusiness, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics in Brazil. On August 25, the Foundation kicked off “Cardano on the Road,” a new institutional outreach initiative for Latin America. First stop: Petrobras headquarters in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil’s largest company, sitting at roughly $90 billion in annual revenue. The idea here is to steadily grow Cardano’s footprint across Latin American enterprises and public institutions in the months ahead, so expect more stops on this road trip. Cardano also confirmed its role as Platinum Sponsor at TOKEN2049 Singapore , taking place October 7–8, the ecosystem’s largest Asia Pacific presence yet. The booth at Marina Bay Sands will showcase 20 ecosystem projects, and the side events are worth circling on your calendar too: a Node Diversity Celebration Day on October 6, and a UTXO Pitch Night on October 7 where founders get the chance to pitch for up to $500K in funding. Full details plus the conference discount code (CARDANOSG279B) are up at token2049.cardano.org . On the thought-leadership side, Foundation CEO Fredrik Gregaard published a piece in Forbes Tech Council digging into blockchain’s transformative potential for smallholder farmers in coffee, cassava, and honey value chains, exploring how verifiable on-chain provenance can improve market access and income stability at scale. And for the builders among us, the Foundation’s Java developer guide for Cardano via BloxBean , shared August 27, drew a lot of community engagement. The message: Java developers can build on Cardano without learning a new language or toolchain, using the same Maven-based workflows and testing infrastructure they already know. No excuses left, Java devs. Lastly, the Foundation is hiring an Ecosystem Governance Coordinator focused on DRep relations and community outreach, a good sign of just how much institutional weight Cardano’s on-chain governance ecosystem is picking up, and how seriously the Foundation is leaning into it. Update from Intersect MBO According to Intersect MBO’s latest weekly update, preparations for the Dijkstra era continue, with work progressing across node development, release readiness and node diversity. Intersect reports that Amaru has achieved its Q3 goal of delivering a relay node binary and is now working toward a block-producing pre-release on Mainnet in late September. The team is also continuing work on conformance, performance and robustness as it moves toward block production. Alongside the development work, Intersect says that Node Diversity Workshops are planned for Singapore on October 6 and London on November 12–13. The workshops are aimed at bringing together node implementation teams, SPOs and other stakeholders involved in the upcoming upgrade. Be on the look out for more updated in the coming weeks. And for those who missed Intersect’s Weekly Round Up X-Spacelive on September 1, don’t worry, as the space has been recorded. The Space covered the latest developments across the organisation and Cardano, with time for community questions and discussion. The recording is available on X. Listen to it here . Read the Board Elections announcement Beyond talks about hard forks, node diversity, and X-Spaces, Intersect MBO has also been making changes to how members interact with the organisation. In its latest update, Intersect highlighted improvements to the Member Area, including a new self-service voting area and an “All members” page where members and associates can connect, view participation badges and committee or Board roles, and maintain their public profiles. Intersect also reports that it has simplified its member verification process by removing the previous address verification requirement. items.title: Digest August 19, 2026: Cardano at TOKEN2049, Rare Evo 2026 Recap, Urgent Governance Call to Action, Rethinking Catalyst Funding, Real-World Impact & Tech Wins, CIP Updates, and more
items.description: Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight: Cardano at TOKEN2049: Cardano is taking over Marina Bay Sands with a massive booth and covering travel and stay expenses for 20 ecosystem projects. Applications are open now. Rare Evo 2026 Recap: Relive the energy of Las Vegas in a recently released short recap showcasing the builders, tech, and community driving the ecosystem forward. Urgent Governance Call to Action: Two critical on-chain votes are on the line, including the 2026 Constitutional Committee update. DReps and SPOs need to act before September 1. Rethinking Catalyst Funding: The new Catalyst Pilot is awarding out grants up to 200k ada based on real-world usage. Plus, applications are live for the Decision Panel. Protocol & Dev Updates: Fresh CIP proposals hit the floor-covering everything from post-quantum ZK signatures to upgraded Plutus Core conformance testing. Ecosystem Alpha & Newsletters: Deep dives into the 120M ADA PRIME treasury approval, L4VA’s instantly popular tokenised silver vault, Hydra v2.3.0, and Ogmios v7. Creator Radar & Builder Tech: Spotlighting agentic commerce breakdowns, Draper University founder updates, Tessera’s on-chain surveys, and enterprise data on Dune. Real-World Impact & Tech Wins: Over 100k Georgian wine bottles go on-chain via Cardano, Gimbalabs wraps its latest hackathon, and Binance Academy drops an Ouroboros deep dive. Intersect’s Latest Moves: The Constitutional Amendment Portal receives its first submissions, real-time treasury tracking goes live, and Nick Clarke steps in as Director of Cardano Technology. All this and more in today’s Digest. Cardano’s TOKEN2049 Booth: Applications Are Now Open Cardano is going big at TOKEN2049 Singapore coming 7-8 October, with its biggest-ever presence. As Platinum sponsor, the Foundation is bringing a 108sqm booth at Marina Bay Sands and looking to fill it with 20 ecosystem projects, plus side events still to be confirmed. The Foundation has launched a dedicated application page at token2049.cardano.org with full details on how to apply. Selected projects don’t just get a spot on the floor, the Foundation covers flights (economy, up to $2,000) and up to three nights’ accommodation for one team member, so it’s a real shot at getting your project in front of the TOKEN2049 crowd without eating the travel cost yourself. Applications close August 25, with selected projects announced September 1. If you’re building on Cardano and want in, don’t wait, but get your application in today. Check the full announcement here . Recap Video: Rare Evo 2026 From 28 to 31 July the Cardano community showed up in force at Rare Evo 2026 in Las Vegas. A short recap video recently dropped, capturing neatly the spirit of the event, and exactly why people keep coming back to this event year after year. Over the four days at the ARIA Resort, Ambassadors, builders, and everyday community members ran demos, talked governance and funding routes, and made the case for why Cardano is still one of the most thoughtful places to build. The video itself is pure energy: booth conversations, stage moments including Kenny Edwards in full astronaut gear talking Carda Station and Daniel Ribar from Catalyst , trading-card sessions, late-night networking, and that unmistakable feeling of people who genuinely like being in the same room together. In a space that often feels noisy, this one’s definitely a reminder of the long game. Yes, the tech matters. Yes, the research matters. Yes, the funding matters, but ultimately it’s the people who keep turning up that truly make the difference. Watch the recap here Two Governance Actions Need Your Vote Before September 1 Intersect MBO recently dropped an urgent reminder that two on-chain governance actions are hanging in the balance. Both of them need community votes before 1 September, 2026. Check out the post here . So here’s what’s at stake. First up… The Protocol Parameter Update. This one would reduce the minimum pool cost to 75 ada and increase Plutus memory limits. Sounds technical, but basically it’s about making it more competitive for stake pools to operate while giving Plutus smart contracts more room to breathe. Right now it’s sitting at just 32.27% DRep support and 2.03% SPO support, way below the 67% and 51% thresholds needed. Check it out here: Reduce minPoolCost to 75 ADA and Increase Plutus Memory Limits Second… The Constitutional Committee 2026 update. This one replaces four committee seats whose terms are expiring with the candidates elected through the recent community vote. Here’s the thing though, if this doesn’t pass before the deadline, the Constitutional Committee would drop below its minimum of five members, and that would effectively pause Cardano’s entire governance process until it’s restored. Not ideal. Currently sitting at just 30.04% DRep support. Full details here: Update Constitutional Committee 2026 Why is this so important? Well… The Committee update is particularly time-sensitive because of a ledger rule. The action sets new members’ terms to expire at Epoch 799, and because of how the math works out, it can only be enacted at Epoch 653. If, as a community, we miss that window, then we’re in trouble. The action will ratify in its final epoch regardless of when votes come in, so don’t wait. DReps and SPOs, head over to gov.tools or DRepTalk and cast your votes. Help Decide What the Catalyst Pilot Funds The Catalyst Pilot is a fresh take on Catalyst funding, offering grants of 50,000 to 200,000 ADA for teams with working products. The twist? Funding is paid out based on real usage they bring to Cardano. Decisions are made by a Decision Panel, and who sits on that panel depends entirely on who applies. Applications are open now. The Catalyst Team is on the lookout for people who have shipped or audited real systems on mainnet, as well as those who have operated, funded, or formally assessed ventures. Here’s the deal: around 12 reviews across late August and early September, an honorarium for taking part, and a straightforward 5-minute application where what you link matters more than how much you write. One thing to note, you can either propose a project or serve on the panel, not both. If you read that and thought “that sounds like me,” then it’s probably worth applying. The Catalyst Team encourages anyone who fits the bill to submit the form and they’ll take it from there. Apply by Monday 25 August → link here Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Updates Robert Phair is back with another snapshot of the Cardano Improvement Proposal process, the mechanism through which any stakeholder can push for changes to the protocol. Some proposals are technical, think address formats or transaction metadata, while others start out conceptual, framed as a Cardano Problem Statement that names a problem before anyone’s landed on a solution. From there, it’s an open review: the ecosystem weighs in, and proposals either build enough momentum to move toward adoption or settle in as reference material for whoever tackles the problem next.. Below is an update on the newly submitted proposals, proposals currently in review, and ones that have recently been completed. New Proposals CIP-0197 candidate: Post-Quantum ZK Signatures for HD Wallets - an intermediate step in achieving post-quantum asset security: by supplementing existing signatures with zero-knowledge proofs of wallet seed phrases CPS-0034 candidate: Extending Plutus Core conformance testing - proposed characteristics of a common framework for Plutus consistency and quality assurance across Cardano’s multiple node types Active Review CIP-0196 candidate: Handle Provider Registry & Resolver CIP-0178 candidate: Merkle Root of Transactions in Block Header CPS-0030 candidate: Quantum-secure settlement layer Completed CIP-0168: More `BuiltinValue` Functions CIP-0172: Self-Usable Transaction Outputs CIP-0183: Conflict-Based Fee Priority in Mempool CPS-0028: Approaches to non-strict UPLC evaluation CPS-0033: DRep Voting Power Concentration Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates On 17 August, 2026, Cardanians has, once again, released its latest Ecosystem Newsletter . This week’s edition highlights the 120 million ADA PRIME treasury approval and what this funding program could mean for Cardano’s DeFi trajectory over the next six months. It also takes a deep dive into the Dijkstra upgrade timeline, with Linear Leios staying on track for a 2026 mainnet debut and Ouroboros Peras release locked in for Q2 2027. Rounding out the highlights, the team covers USDM’s launch on the Midnight privacy chain via VIA Labs and how that all benefits Cardano’s expanding interoperability footprint. Cardano Newsletter: Weekly Cardano Digest #139 And that’s not all, because also on August 17, Lucas Macchiavelli has dropped his latest Weekly Cardano Digest #139 . This week’s edition shines a spotlight on three standout developments shaking up the ecosystem. First up, L4VA Technologies and Toto Finance have deployed an institutional-grade tokenised silver vault directly on Cardano’s mainnet, where each NFT represents one ounce of certified, insured physical silver. The vault hit 76% capacity just moments after launch, signalling serious real-world demand for asset tokenisation on Cardano. Second, Hydra version 2.3.0 dropped with some meaningful snapshot processing improvements and YAML-based node configuration, making life easier for node operators. And third, TxPipe announced that Ogmios v7 is now available as a managed endpoint on Demeter, bringing Dijkstra era support and multi-region infrastructure to developers with zero operational overhead. Check out the full issue at Lucas’s newsletter site: Weekly Cardano Digest #139 Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators This week, we’re shining a light on some of Cardano’s community-driven content creators and ecosystem contributors. From reaction videos and founder journey updates to educational threads on cross-chain interoperability, enterprise data interviews, and a developer deep dive into on-chain surveys, these individuals and teams continue to help make Cardano more accessible, informative, and engaging for builders and community members alike. Here are a few recent highlights from across the ecosystem:: Angry Crypto Show (Cardano Ambassador) recently published a reaction video breaking down Charles Hoskinson’s comments on agentic commerce as crypto’s next major growth area, the case for a simpler and safer narrative to attract trillions in capital and billions of users, major Hydra performance upgrades, and more. Watch it here Sticking with the founder journey theme, Peter Bui (Learn Cardano), also a Cardano Ambassador, shared Day Zero and Day One updates from the Draper University Genesis Pre-Accelerator. In the video he shared how Day Zero included meeting the cohort of founders and all of the early excitement heading into the program. Part of Day one was also the Cardano introduction, Draper’s 61-year startup history, pitch deck work, mentor session bookings, and the official start of the VC journey toward pitching to Tim Draper and his team: Watch Day Zero here and Watch Day One here Two other community educators also published threads this week breaking down the significance of the Cardano–Injective IBC testnet connection for a wider audience. @dawing_x offered a clear ELI5-style breakdown on what a direct on-chain rail between Cardano and Injective means for users, specifically the ability to move assets between chains without a centralised bridge: Read it here . Separately, @Cryptolab06 published an explainer thread framing the IBC connection as a demonstration of what real blockchain interoperability should look like in practice: Read it here And that’s not all, because Linda (CryptoFly) also released two videos this cycle. In the first, she compares Cardano’s Bitcoin DeFi plans with Sui’s similar efforts (centered on the Hashi platform and its growing list of institutional partners), examining security models, traction, and which chain has the stronger shot at capturing Bitcoin’s trillions in capital: Watch it here . In her second video, she really took her time and dived into Cardano’s approval of a higher Net Change Limit (NCL), which opens the door to spending up to half a billion ada from the treasury - with AlphaGrowth’s 120 million ADA PRIME proposal next in Cardano’s DeFi revamp, and what it all reveals about Cardano’s governance and growth priorities. Worth a watch!: Watch it here Community Learning & Developer Engagement During a recent Developer Office Hours, Matthieu Pizenberg walked through on-chain surveys on Cardano, introducing the Tessera project and the associated CIP-0179 proposal, which defines a standardized format for conducting verifiable, transparent surveys directly on Cardano’s blockchain. The conversation covers how Tessera leverages Cardano’s extended UTXO model for survey integrity, the architecture behind the implementation, and the path from community proposal to on-chain reality: Watch it here In this episode of Let’s Talk Cardano, the conversation turns to Nia Whitaker, Blockchain Success Lead at Dune, on making blockchain data usable for every kind of enterprise team. It covers what changed once Cardano’s data became available on Dune, how the platform gives businesses a full picture instead of isolated transactions, why removing technical barriers matters for non-technical teams, and how accessible data is what ultimately earns enterprise trust. Watch it here Updates from the Cardano Foundation Cardano is going big at TOKEN2049 Singapore, happening October 7-8, with its biggest-ever presence at the conference. The Foundation has launched a dedicated application page at token2049.cardano.org , where it’s inviting up to 20 ecosystem projects to apply for a spot at the exhibition booth. Applications close August 25, so if you’re a Cardano project, don’t sit on this one, get your application in. Check out the full announcement here . On the adoption side, more than 30 Georgian wineries have now anchored provenance records for over 100,000 wine bottles on Cardano, using the Foundation’s open-source OriginateNavio reference implementation. With European wine counterfeiting estimated to cost €2.8 billion annually, this is solving a real problem rather than chasing a nice-to-have, and the timing lines up well: EU Digital Product Passport mandates are on the horizon, and the Foundation put together a thread making the case that Cardano’s permissionless design, open standards, and interoperability make it a natural fit for DPP implementation. Worth a read. Check out the link here . The Foundation also backed the Gimbalabs Piece of Pie Hackathon with 20,000 ADA and a dedicated Cardano track for the 12-week builder programme. Teams that qualified got to pitch to Draper Dragon, and the results landed recently. link . For anyone still unclear on Cardano’s fundamentals, the Foundation partnered with Binance Academy on an educational thread breaking down Ouroboros, Cardano’s peer-reviewed proof-of-stake consensus. It’s part of the Cardano Fundamentals course now live on Binance Academy, and it does a solid job of explaining how Ouroboros gets proof-of-work-level security at a fraction of the energy cost. Good one to send newcomers. Check out the details here . One more deadline worth flagging: the Catalyst 2026 Pilot application window is closing fast. 2.5 million ADA is up for grabs across 10 to 15 teams, with funding per team ranging from 50,000 to 200,000 ADA, focused on oracles, stablecoins, programmable tokens, and on-chain identity. Details here Update from Intersect MBO As per the Intersect’s weekly update of 14 August, 2026, the Constitutional Amendment Portal (CAP) is getting quite some love from the community, with four submissions rolling in after its alpha launch at Rare Evo. We’re talking three Constitutional Amendment Proposals and one Constitutional Issue Statement. The whole idea is that anyone can connect their wallet and jump straight into proposing and refining changes to Cardano’s foundational governance document. If you’re keen to get involved, the working group meets every Thursday at 09:00 UTC. Full details are in Intersect Weekly Update #124 . The 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract (TRSC) tracking dashboard is now live, and honestly, it’s a pretty big deal for transparency. Community members can now publicly monitor treasury withdrawals administered by Intersect in real time. No more guessing games, everything’s out in the open. Here’s the announcement . Speaking of transparency, the 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract (TRSC) tracking dashboard recently went live. Community members can now publicly monitor treasury withdrawals administered by Intersect in real time. Check it out here . And last but definitely not least, Intersect has brought Nick Clarke on board as Director of Cardano Technology. The guy’s a mathematician and functional programmer who’s been in the Cardano trenches since 2018, leading the Byron-era rewrite and most recently serving as Director of Engineering at Tweag. He’ll be steering technical coordination for the Dijkstra era upgrade, working across Intersect’s committees and the broader contributor ecosystem. Big things ahead. Check out the announcement here .
