Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight Pyth Pro Goes Live on Cardano: Institutional-grade pricing infrastructure is now live on Cardano, bringing millisecond price updates and low-latency market data for DeFi, synthetics, and trading applications. Spotlight on the CIP Process: A closer look at Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIPs), the open-source standards process helping shape Cardano’s technical evolution and ecosystem innovation. Yoroi Rebrands to SecondFi: EMURGO announced Yoroi’s evolution into SecondFi, expanding beyond a wallet into a broader self-custody neofinance platform. Intersect MBO Updates: Intersect shared final committee election results and confirmed Node v11.0.1 is now mainnet hard fork ready for the upcoming van Rossem upgrade. C ommunity Learning & Governance: Recent sessions explored DRep participation, intent-based dApps, x402 integration, and Cardano infrastructure tooling. Cardano Foundation Updates: The Foundation shared new partnerships, compliance integrations, digital identity education, and discussions on trust infrastructure and interoperability. All this and more in today’s Digest. Pyth Pro Now Live on Cardano From the Pentad’s first Critical Infrastructure deal announced on December 11, 2025, to full production deployment just under five months later, Pyth Pro is now live on Cardano and the gap is closed. Millisecond price updates. Sub-100ms end-to-end latency. Coverage across crypto, equities, FX, and commodities. Data sourced directly from 125+ institutional publishers, not scraped APIs or opaque aggregators. This is the pricing infrastructure that synthetics, lending markets, and derivatives actually need: fast, accurate, and manipulation-resistant. The same class of tooling used by professional trading desks is now available to Cardano builders. As per the announcement update, Indigo Protocol is the first integration, with more protocols soon to follow. For the full announcement text, click here . Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIP) Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIPs) fulfil the same role for Cardano as the standards of other blockchains, including BIPs for Bitcoin and EIPs for Ethereum . CIPs document how developers are improving fundamental technologies and conventions: expanding the field of creative and commercial possibility through standards submitted by both core projects and independent developers. Once passing our decentralised review process, a CIP becomes a resource to either advance the Cardano blockchain itself or build products & markets upon it. These proposals are open source and can be improved upon by anyone with interest & knowledge in that area. The CIP process encourages observation and participation across the entire Cardano community. To get involved: See the CIPs Wiki to learn how it works (from introductory to expert level); Visit the GitHub CIPs repository and click Watch for real-time updates on CIPs. For a deeper dive into CIPs, we recommend the following resources as well: https://cips.cardano.org for more information about the CIP process, including an overview of CIPs Medium Article by Cardano Ambassador Robert Phair: Cardano Improvement Proposals (CIPs) — Introduction from an Insider Intersect Committee Election Results The April 2026 Intersect Committee Elections are wrapped up, and according to the official update from Intersect MBO, it was a busy one. As per the announcement, 102 candidates stood for 37 seats across eight committees, with 187 unique members casting a total of 3,967 ballots, representing 24.8% of eligible voters. The update also notes that following the close of voting, Intersect carried out a routine post-election review alongside an independent third-party audit by Dquadrant, with results confirmed and additional steps being taken to strengthen membership verification going forward. For the full breakdown of elected members, vote tallies per committee, and everything else, check out the full post on the Intersect MBO website . Yoroi Wallet Rebranding Into SecondFi On April 22, 2026, EMURGO announced that Yoroi Wallet will evolve into “SecondFi,”! At this point you may be wondering what that is. Well…Secondfi is a self-custody neofinance platform. According to the announcement, the transition expands Yoroi beyond a traditional wallet experience, combining spending, sending, staking, trading, and asset management into a single platform while making sure users remain in control of their assets. EMURGO noted that existing wallets, delegated stake, rewards, and DRep participation will remain unchanged after the app has been upgraded to SecondFi. The company also emphasized that users do not need to move their assets. Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators This week, we’re shining a light on some of Cardano’s community-driven content creators and ecosystem contributors. Across interviews, educational sessions, technical deep dives, and community discussions, these individuals and teams continue to help make Cardano more accessible, informative, and engaging for builders and community members alike. Here are a few recent highlights from across the ecosystem: Rare Network The team at Rare Network recently released a short clip consisting of multiple interviews with the project leads sharing from the heart what Cardano means to them, why live are so important - basically explaining why they’re so passionate about Cardano. Watch it here. Watch It Here Powered by Cardano Alfred has recently released another set of interviews conducted during the Gitex Africa, Morocco Edition. During this episode he sat down with Ese Williams, the Head of Marketing at Remo Star, to learn of her vision for Cardano in Africa. Check out her video here on X . Community Learning & Developer Engagement Developer Office Hours Participation in the Cardano Developer Office Hours continues to grow, with developers actively tuning in to learn, share knowledge, and interact live with participants. Recent sessions featured: Recap: Cardano Education in Schools – Nimrod Ndebele Exhibition (8 May 2026)**- WIMS Cardano has promoted Cardano education in high schools since 2022 through coding, AI and blockchain outreach. At the Nimrod Ndebele Secondary School Careers Exhibition on 8 May 2026 in Duduza, Nigel, South Africa, the team showcased Cardano-based learning empowering learners and future developers and entrepreneurs. Former students now mentor others and completed the EBU Plutus Haskell programme, reflecting long-term impact. The founder of WIMS, a Cardano Ambassador, shared a vision for education-driven Cardano adoption. Read the full recap here . Roundtable Talk: DRep Participation in Focus - On May 4, 2026, the Cardano Community hosted Roundtable Talk #37: DRep Participation in Focus. This Roundtable focused on DRep participation and its role within Cardano governance. The panel, consisting of Governance Champions, Nicolas Cerny, Hix, Ken-Erik, Nana Safo, Rodrigo Pacini, Thiago Nunes, and Logan Panchot sat down for an honest and constructive conversation about where Cardano governance stands today and where it can go. Topics ranged from strengthening accountability and transparency among DReps, to practical ideas like better governance tools in wallets, smarter delegation mechanics, and specialized coordination layers that bring domain expertise into the process. The full episode can be viewed here . Building Intent-Based DApps: GCScript DSL & Universal Dapp Connector (UDC) - In this session of the Cardano Developer Office Hours, Adriano Fiorenza, Founder & Developer of GameChanger Wallet, demonstrates how to build intent-based DApps on Cardano using GCScript DSL and the Universal Dapp Connector (UDC). The session focuses on creating client-side, user-first Web3 applications that integrate Cardano open protocols through links, QR codes, and NFC with minimal dependencies. He also covers the shift to intent-based models, streamlined DApp logic with GCScript DSL, and how UDC simplifies connectivity through standard web technologies without required installations. Missed it? Watch here . x402 on Cardano: Version 2 Standard & Integration | Developers Office Hour - In this session of the Cardano Developer Office Hours, Fabian Bormann, Head of Ecosystem Engineering at the Cardano Foundation, explores the x402 standard, covering the evolution of version 2 and the ongoing progress toward integration with the Cardano blockchain. He provides a technical overview of the x402 specification, highlights key updates introduced in version 2, and outlines the roadmap for full ecosystem integration and future development. Watch here . Additional details also shared here by the Masumi team Cardano’s Next-Gen Infrastructure: Andamio v2 & AI Agentic Workflows - In this recap video, the Cardano team shares highlights from JCON EUROPE 2026, the premier in-person Java community conference organized by the Java User Group Oberpfalz in collaboration with JAVAPRO Magazine. Represented by developers and the engineering team from the Cardano Foundation, the recap covers conversations with Java developers, discussions around blockchain scalability, and the tools needed to help the Java community begin building in Web3 on Cardano. Watch here . From community storytelling and governance discussions to developer education and technical exploration, these initiatives continue to reflect the collaborative spirit of the Cardano ecosystem. If you’d like to stay informed on upcoming sessions, interviews, and ecosystem updates, be sure to follow the creators and channels featured above and subscribe for future content. Updates from the Cardano Foundation The Cardano Foundation has shared several recent updates, highlighting ecosystem progress across institutional partnerships, compliance infrastructure, education, and digital identity. The Foundation announced a strategic partnership with the University of Brasília (UnB), launching the first Cardano Project Development Lab in Latin America. Combining the Foundation’s global expertise in blockchain infrastructure with UnB’s academic leadership and proximity to Brazil’s federal government, an institution that has educated generations of public servants, ministers, and diplomats, the collaboration aims to unlock new models for transparency, efficiency, and digital trust in the public sector. The lab will serve as a multidisciplinary innovation hub at the intersection of public blockchain infrastructure, artificial intelligence, IoT, digital identity, and governance solutions. Read the full announcement here . Besides that, Cardano has been fully integrated into Scorechain’s compliance and investigation platform, adding support for ada and Cardano native tokens across risk scoring, entity attribution, and transaction monitoring, all built for Cardano’s UTXO model. Multi-chain teams can now monitor, analyze, and investigate Cardano transactions within the same unified workflow used for other major networks. As the Foundation’s Pierre Kaklamanos put it, “the future of finance is multi-chain, and compliance infrastructure is how blockchains earn institutional trust.” Read more here . The Foundation also published a new case study, Reeve for Better Account Systems , building on Reeve’s growing track record in verifiable financial reporting. Reeve records financial data directly on-chain, creating immutable and transparent records that stakeholders can independently verify, simplifying audits and fostering confidence through accurate, tamper-resistant data. This follows the milestone of completing the world’s first cryptographically attested on-chain audit in collaboration with Grant Thornton Switzerland. Explore the case study here . Cardano Academy has also launched a new free course titled KERI and the Future of Digital Identity , covering the protocol behind Veridian, the Foundation’s open-source digital identity platform. The course introduces learners to Autonomic Trust, a model where identity is self-certifying, portable, and mathematically verifiable without intermediaries, and spans 18 focused units covering the KERI protocol, verifiable credentials, and the vLEI system as a real-world, ISO-standardized implementation operating globally. It is designed for enterprise decision-makers, developers, and legal and compliance professionals alike, equipping a broad range of practitioners with the foundations needed to engage confidently with the evolving decentralized identity ecosystem. Explore the course here In a recent episode of Let’s Talk Cardano, the Foundation spoke with Douglas Heintzman, Chief Catalyst at the Blockchain Research Institute and CEO of Syncura, about how digital trust infrastructure is shaping the next phase of the global economy. The discussion explores how blockchain enables trusted data and transactions, and how identity, credentials, and payment systems connect to reduce friction across industries. The conversation also covers governance, interoperability, and how embedding trust at the infrastructure level can support more efficient processes and real-world adoption at scale. The full episode can be re-watched on YouTube or on Spotify . Finally, the March 2026 activities report covers a busy month across regulatory developments, governance votes, institutional engagements, and continued ecosystem growth. On the regulatory front, the SEC, with CFTC input, included ada as an example of a digital commodity in its new interpretation of digital assets, a classification suggesting the token’s value derives from network functionality rather than any central issuing entity. CEO Frederik Gregaard also held conversations in New York with Yahoo Finance, GBBC, and Fintech TV, while Chief Legal Officer Nicolas Jacquemart participated in policy dialogue at Merkle Meet DC 2026. Read the full update here . Update from Intersect MBO The April 2026 Intersect Committee Elections have now concluded, and according to the official update published on May 8, 2026, the turn out was great. As per the announcement, 102 candidates stood for 37 seats across eight committees, with 187 unique members casting a total of 3,967 ballots, representing 24.8% of eligible voters. Following the close of voting, Intersect carried out a routine post-election review alongside an independent third-party audit by Dquadrant, with results confirmed and additional steps being taken to strengthen membership verification going forward. To everyone who ran, voted, or engaged in the process, the community’s participation is what gives it its legitimacy. Read the full election results here . items.description: Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight Cardano becomes Official x402 Chain: Cardano has been integrated into the x402 standard, enabling native, automated, and verifiable on-chain payments between AI agents and services. Blockfrost Integrates Filecoin Premium Storage: This is a major upgrade to developer infrastructure, allowing Cardano developers to utilize Filecoin’s global, decentralized network for a robust and reliable data backup without infrastructure overhead. Intersect MBO Governance & Technical Updates: Progress on the Van Rossem Upgrade is advancing with Node v11.0 nearing Mainnet-readiness. Governance updates include the release of the 2026-27 Budget Proposal and the start of Constitutional Committee candidate registration on May 1. Cardano at Java Conference : At JCON 2026 in Cologne, the Cardano Foundation team bridged the gap to the Java ecosystem, turning developer skepticism into adoption through technical showcases of the JuLC compiler and Digital Product Passports. All this and more in today’s Digest. Cardano Becomes Official x402 Chain Cardano has been officially integrated into the x402 standard, marking a significant milestone for the ecosystem. The x402 protocol (originally developed by Coinbase) enables native, automated, and verifiable on-chain pay-to-access payments between AI agents and services. The x402 Foundation officially merged the Pull Request for the Cardano Specification, making Cardano an official x402 chain . Furthermore, the optional inclusion of the Masumi Smart Contract enhances the Cardano implementation, providing powerful features such as Identity, Refunds & Disputes, Decision Logging, and Registry. This integration is particularly applicable to agent-to-agent payment challenges, simplifying Web3 payments for all users. Details on X . Blockfrost Integrates Filecoin Premium Storage for Cardano Developers Blockfrost has integrated Filecoin’s premium storage tier, allowing Cardano developers to utilize Filecoin’s global, decentralized network for a robust and reliable data backup. This collaboration, which is backed by the Filecoin Foundation, establishes a verifiable, distributed storage layer across independent providers. For data-driven applications on Cardano, this represents a major reliability upgrade that enhances data redundancy and security. Developers can adopt this premium tier with no infrastructure overhead and without requiring any changes to their existing workflows. For the full details, read the original article . Paris Blockchain Week The Paris Blockchain Week was a major success for Cardano, where the ecosystem showcased a remarkable presence. As part of a coordinated appearance, 25 different Cardano projects presented themselves under a single brand and utilized a shared booth. This unified approach allowed them to communicate a cohesive narrative to stakeholders, including institutional clients, retail investors, developers, and partners. The goal was to demonstrate the strength and cohesion of the Cardano industry to the wider blockchain community. The Paris Blockchain Week video is now available**, view here. ** Cardano at JCON 2026: Bridging Java and Blockchain The Cardano Foundation’s presence at JCON in Cologne marked a significant shift in how the enterprise Java community views decentralized technology. Moving past the “blockchain is a scam” narrative of previous years, the 2026 event focused on technical substance and real-world utility. Key Highlights A Serious Audience: JCON was a “learning-first” environment. Unlike typical crypto events, the halls were empty during sessions as thousands of experienced Java developers focused on presentations. The Bridge (JuLC): The biggest technical takeaway was the JuLC (Java-to-UPLC) compiler. It allows developers to write both off-chain and on-chain code in Java, removing the barrier to building Plutus V3 smart contracts. Check it: https://github.com/bloxbean/julc Real-World Use Cases: Fabian Bormann’s session , “Building a Digital Product Passport with Java and Cardano,” demonstrated how blockchain solves transparency and compliance needs in enterprise supply chains. From “Coin” to Infrastructure: Conversations at the booth often started with skepticism but ended with developers realizing Cardano’s potential as a backbone for backend enterprise systems. Looking Forward The JCON team has become a strong ally, actively helping us connect with established Java ecosystem partners. The participation of this year makes a dedicated hands-on workshop for 2027 the logical next step to deepen this integration. Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates The latest update shared by Cardanians focuses on important advancements in infrastructure, project visibility, and marketing governance. Developer infrastructure is seeing an improvement as Blockfrost has integrated Filecoin’s premium storage, allowing Cardano developers to utilize Filecoin’s global network for reliable data backup without extra infrastructure overhead. For better project visibility, the blockchain explorer Cexplorer launched a new Project Page to consolidate all projects building on Cardano in one central location. The goal is to provide users with easy access to projects, their products, and on-chain connections (including assets, scripts, and DReps). Finally, the Serviceplan Group , a major advertising agency with notable clients such as BMW, Netflix, and LEGO, submitted a 21 million ADA Marketing Proposal to the Intersect Budget Process. This proposal aims to make Cardano, which stands on strong technical foundations, more appealing to enterprise decision-makers. For all the details and more, view here the X thread . Cardano Governance: Intense Week (April 20–26) The week of April 20–26 saw intense Cardano governance activity. The Cardano Foundation hosted live AMAs on X discussing the Cardano Summit 2026 treasury withdrawal. In parallel, Input Output (IOG) submitted nine treasury withdrawal requests totaling 162,142,627 ADA for various initiatives like Cardano Maintenance and Cardano Upgrades (full details: https://momentum.cardano.iog.io/ ). High-stakes submissions also continued through Intersect’s Budget Process using the Hydra voting tool , including several multi-million ADA proposals for marketing and core infrastructure. This has been a particularly demanding week for everyone involved in governance. Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators This week, we’re highlighting some of Cardano’s content creators, community members who help keep the ecosystem informed and engaged. Whether through tutorials, blogs, or thought-provoking discussions, they contribute valuable context and keep the conversation moving. Here are a few creators making an impact: Peter Bui (Learn Cardano) Peter Bui (Learn Cardano), Cardano Ambassador, SPO of ADAOZ Pool, and creator of the Learn Cardano YouTube channel, recently released a new video breaking down four Cardano Partner Chains. Watch it here. Watch It Here Cardano Feed Cardano Feed is one of the fastest and most consistent sources for daily news and video highlights across the entire ecosystem. They cover governance updates, technical developments, Partner Chains, and key ecosystem news in a clear and timely way. Perfect for staying up to date quickly. Check them out on X and cardanofeed.com . Community Learning & Developer Engagement Developer Office Hours Participation in the Cardano Developer Office Hours continues to grow, with developers actively tuning in to learn, share knowledge, and interact live with participants. Recent sessions featured: Governance Hour #3 – Deep Dive Into Pebble + Gerolamo - HLabs Budget - This session explored HLabs’ 2026 budget proposal with Michele Nuzzi, founder of Harmonic Laboratories. The discussion provided a comprehensive overview of two key projects focusing on expanding Cardano’s developer ecosystem: Gerolamo, a TypeScript-based alternative node client, and Pebble, a programming language and toolkit for DApp development. These Governance Hours facilitate interactive discussion, encouraging stakeholders to ask critical questions to better understand the proposal’s nuances and support informed voting. Full summary and recording . Scalus Emulator – In-Memory Cardano Node for JVM/JS/TS Testing - In this session, Alex Nemish and Serhii Lekariev from Lantr introduced the Scalus In-Memory Emulator . This tool is designed to drastically accelerate the development cycle for smart contracts and dApp logic by simulating a Cardano node and its ledger state directly within JVM, JavaScript, and TypeScript environments. This in-memory approach enables fast testing and instant feedback, eliminating the overhead of a full local node or testnet and is easily integrated into local development and CI/CD pipelines. Watch here . Building Faster on Cardano: Exploring SIDAN Lab Developer Tools with Hinson Wong - In this Developers Office Hour, we sit down with Hinson Wong, Co-founder & CEO of DeltaDeFi and SIDAN Lab, to explore the powerful suite of open-source tools they’ve built for the Cardano ecosystem. Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard was highly visible this week, contributing to key industry reports and discussions that frame Cardano as a leader in institutional-grade, regulated blockchain infrastructure. Frederik contributed to the latest CV VC Crypto Valley Top 50 & Ecosystem Report , which highlights the ongoing evolution of Crypto Valley into an ecosystem where infrastructure, regulation, and real-world implementation are converging. The report features Cardano among the leading blockchain networks by market capitalization, recognizing the Foundation’s role in supporting its development and adoption. Frederik emphasized that the next phase of asset tokenization will rely on regulated, audit-ready infrastructure rather than experimentation alone, a direction that aligns perfectly with Cardano’s focus on resilient, research-driven infrastructure that enables transparency, accountability, and scalable real-world use cases. Read the full update here . Furthermore, Frederik participated in an interview with the Global Blockchain Business Council (GBBC) at the NYSE to discuss the future trajectory of blockchain adoption. The conversation centered on advanced topics, including agentic AI, digital identity, quantum-secure infrastructure, and the transition of public permissionless blockchains into critical infrastructure for regulated markets. The Foundation welcomed guests Joshua Krüger, Head of Growth at DFX Swiss, and Ralph Hofacker, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Brick Towers. The trio discussed the successful integration of ADA payments in over 130 Spar supermarkets across Switzerland. The conversation explored the technical infrastructure powering Open CryptoPay, which facilitates real-time interaction between crypto and traditional fiat systems. They highlighted the significant benefits of using a public blockchain for payments, such as dramatically faster transaction times and lower fees compared to existing payment rail methods, providing clear evidence of Cardano’s practical utility in a high-volume consumer environment. Candidate registration for the Constitutional Committee elections is set to begin on May 1. Voting for the current Intersect Committee elections will conclude on May 1. The Civics Committee launched a Governance Incentives Working Group tasked with developing recommendations to reward governance actors, including DReps and Committee members. Pragma Project Committee: Applications Open For New Pragma Projects On April 11, 2026, the Pragma Project Committee announced that applications are officially open for new open-source projects to join the Pragma ecosystem. As a non-profit association dedicated to the long-term sustainability of Cardano’s software stack, Pragma is seeking developers and maintainers who are building critical open-source tools that benefit the broader community. What makes this initiative interesting is the collaborative environment that it offers for essential projects that receive institutional support, governance, and resources necessary to thrive as public goods. To be eligible for this level of support, projects must demonstrate a clear benefit to the Cardano network and in full alignment with Pragma’s mission of supporting high-quality, open-source infrastructure. The selection process is overseen by the Project Committee, which evaluates submissions based on their technical merit and impact on the ecosystem. Those interested in applying must submit their proposals before the deadline on Friday, May 8, at 8:00 PM UTC. Application Form can be found here . Volatility Shares: ADA ETF On April 1, 2026, Volatility Shares announced through their X announcement the launch of a new Cardano ETF, marking another step in bringing ada exposure into traditional financial markets. The ETF will be referenced under the ticker CRDD and is part of a broader rollout of crypto-linked ETFs that also includes Stellar and Chainlink. According to TapTools in a recent Medium post , “the fund is structured to gain this exposure through futures contracts and other derivative instruments rather than holding ada directly. This places it within an established exchange-traded product framework while allowing ada to be represented inside a regulated financial vehicle.” This approach allows the ETF to operate within existing regulatory frameworks while still tracking ada’s performance, effectively bridging the gap between traditional finance and blockchain-based assets. By packaging ada into a familiar investment vehicle, Volatility Shares is lowering the barrier to entry and potentially expanding Cardano’s reach to a new class of market participants. Buidler Fest Argentina 2026 Recap From the first event in Toulouse, France in 2024, to its second edition in Da Nang, Vietnam in 2025, the Cardano Buidler Fest returned for its third edition this year in Buenos Aires, Argentina in 2026, bringing together Cardano developers from around the world for in-person collaboration, technical deep dives, and hands-on problem solving. Two days of pure buidler activity. Topics covered at this year’s event included node development, protocol design, determinism, and Cardano’s infrastructure as a foundation for secure, verifiable, enterprise-grade systems. Buidler Fest Argentina was organized by TxPipe, Ambassadors Mauro Andreoli and Lucas Macchiavelli, funded by Project Catalyst, and sponsored by Cardano Foundation, IO Group, Intersect MBO, the Cardano Ambassador Program, and Midnight. For a full recap of the event, including voices from the developer community, view the episode here . Roundtable Talk: The State of Cardano DeFi On Monday, April 13, 2026 the Cardano Community hosted another Roundtable Talk session whereby multiple ecosystem contributors came together to explore the current state of Cardano DeFi. The discussion was focused on several areas shaping user experience and ecosystem growth - areas including trading efficiency, slippage, liquidity depth, institutional participation (the need for institutional multi-sig capabilities), and overall market usability. This was certainly one of the most heated Roundtable Talks thus far, with strong and sometimes opposing views surfacing throughout the discussion. At the table were Jenny Brito, Leem( also known as Joker), VESPR Wallet), Liqwid Finance, Elder Millennial, Blockjock, Tim Bruckmann, Dano Finance, Rusty (also known as Falling Icarus), and Phil DiSarro. Joining the session was Michele Nuzzi, Founder of Harmonic Laboratories. With growing interest in alternative node clients, the discussion explored Gerolamo, a TypeScript-based Cardano node, and Pebble, a programming language and dApp development toolkit. For him, it’s less about price action and more about how governance gives direction to the structure that code builds. items.title: Cardano Summit 2026 + TOKEN2049: Treasury Proposal FAQ
items.description: The Cardano Foundation, together with EMURGO, has submitted a treasury withdrawal proposal requesting 14,076,539 ada (approximately USD 3,659,900) to fund a dual-event strategy in Singapore from October 5-8, 2026: the Cardano Summit 2026 and a Premier Title Sponsorship at TOKEN2049. This FAQ addresses the most commonly raised questions and community feedback regarding the proposal’s budget, strategic rationale, accountability, and governance structure. 1. Why has the Cardano Summit budget increased from the USD 1.2M projected last year to approximately USD 2.8M (before ticket sales and sponsor deduction). What changed? In 2025 we assumed a USD 1.2M budget for the Cardano Summit 2026 supplemented by the previous year’s revenue. This informed our decision to continue to operate with a similar scope and in a similar market environment to Berlin. After much deliberation and in light of several positive ecosystem developments, we decided that a more ambitious strategy combined with a Token2049 presence made sense in a bear market, the message: No matter the circumstances, Cardano is open for business. This led us to a USD 2.5M request from the Treasury for a total Cardano Summit budget of USD 2.813M after the deduction of 2025 ticket sales revenue of USD 313K. We are not including CF costs of organizing. The following ecosystem developments were drivers of our decision to go bigger: The Cardano 2030 strategic vision aligns well with a global event presence for blockchain and finance. Integrations such as USDCx and LayerZero interoperability demand institutional visibility for a solid ROI. The same holds for other positive developments such as the conjunction of Cardano and AI agents, the rollout of CIP113 for tokenization, the progress on bitcoin bridging, ETFs, etc. Singapore is a global financial center and the location firmly positions Cardano in front of international banks, asset managers, and regulators. In terms of the budget increase, there are three main factors at play: Singapore is a much more expensive location than Berlin. Vendor costs are higher, logistical costs are higher, catering costs are higher, etc. Finding sponsors for a Cardano focused event in this market environment will be exceedingly difficult. Based on 2025, we have budgeted for slightly more, but we cannot reasonably assume that sponsorships will increase proportionally to the overall cost. Ticket prices are lower overall, particularly for the community (see question 9 below), reflecting the feedback we received last year. 2. Why combine the 2026 Cardano Summit and Token2049? Scheduling the Summit alongside Token2049 expands access for the Cardano community in Asia and encourages direct engagement with global markets and institutional players. This creates significant synergies and is ultimately what makes the Cardano Summit proposal worthwhile. The institutional and media exposure that TOKEN2049’s 25,000+ audience provides creates the type of reach that the Cardano ecosystem cannot replicate on its own. Further arguments for a combined event include: Access to a massive institutional and developer audience already gathered in Singapore. The Title Sponsorship delivers priority booth selection (108 sqm – the second largest at the event), a dedicated mini-stage for Cardano builders, a 15-minute mainstage keynote, 25 tickets, lead-scanning tools, and social media promotion across TOKEN2049’s channels. The cancellation of TOKEN2049 2026 in Dubai will increase demand for Singapore. Other tier 1 ecosystems host flagship events alongside TOKEN2049. 3. Why Singapore for the 2026 Cardano Summit? We believe that 2026 marks a crucial period for accelerating Cardano’s adoption. We chose Singapore, a global financial hub, to strategically place Cardano and its ecosystem builders before a massive institutional and enterprise audience focused on blockchain. We are also excited to bring the Cardano Summit to the APAC region for the first time, spotlighting the work of our local builders and projects in the region for the wider Cardano Community and global ecosystem. 4. What accountability and oversight mechanisms are in place for the funds? This proposal includes layers of accountability that go beyond previous treasury withdrawals: Smart contract administration: Funds are administered via open-source, audited Sundae Labs treasury contracts. After withdrawal, ada is immediately split between CF and EMURGO with pre-configured milestone-based payment schedules. DQuadrant, Intersect, NMKR, and Sundae Labs serve as the Oversight Committee with authority to pause, resume, or modify milestones. Each vendor contract has two milestones: a kickoff payment and a final payment released only after proof of event delivery and an updated budget report. Public dashboard: treasurywithdrawals.cardanofoundation.org - A community-facing dashboard provides real-time visibility on fund flow and KPI tracking. The proposal makes provision for independent audits and engaging an auditor (Grand Thornton audited the 2025 Summit). The vendor contracts are not delegated to any SPO or DRep, as required by the Cardano Constitution (Article II, Section 7). 5. What happens to unused funds or if ada appreciates? The proposal includes provisions for the repayment of funds to the Treasury If the events are cancelled before vendor payments are due, the balance (after deducting costs already incurred) will be returned to the Treasury. If events are executed successfully but total expenses fall below the requested amount, unspent ada will be returned to the Treasury within six months. If the ada price appreciates between proposal submission and event execution — and the appreciation is not offset by necessary event expenses — the upside will be returned to the Treasury within six months. Revenue generated from the 2026 Summit (target: USD 450,000) will be ring-fenced for 2027 event planning. 6. Where can I read the results of the Summit 2025 and its related regional tech events? The results are all linked to the proposal and were published last March, we are linking the blog here again for your review. 7. What is the Cardano Foundation’s interest in this? The Cardano Foundation’s goal is advancing the adoption of blockchain across industries. Since the broader remit of the 2025 Summit was introduced, incorporating industry leaders and blockchain pioneers on stage debating important cross industry topics - Cardano has enjoyed: Increased opportunities for showcasing projects to enterprises, governments and analysts, resulting in new or continued collaborations in multiple countries across web3, finance, pharma, IT, education, food and luxury goods industries, including MembersCap, Draper University, The European Commission, German Parliament, Hamburger Volksbank and more. An elevated profile as a result of broader media engagement opportunities across mainstream media such as the WSJ, Bloomberg, Fintech TV, Forbes and CNBC and Crypto Media including Cointelegraph, CoinDesk, BTC Echo and more. Therefore CF’s interest is strategic: a successful Summit strengthens the Cardano ecosystem, which is CF’s core mission. 8. What are the specific KPIs the community can hold CF and EMURGO accountable to? Key Performance Indicators are benchmarks against which the Community can measure the success of the proposal, and are the targets which we are working to achieve. The proposal includes detailed KPIs across multiple categories (see Section 7). Key targets include: Summit : 1,200 total attendees; 700 senior executives and decision-makers; 250 enterprise marketing qualified leads; 50 strategic meeting bookings (45-day post-event); 700 earned media pieces; 1 billion+ digital reach; 2,000 new Cardano subscribers. TOKEN 2049 : 1,440 contacts engaged at the booth; 15 new strategic collaborations; 8 expert panels or keynote speaker opportunities; 200 Cardano wallet sign-ups; 200 Cardano Academy subscribers. Hackathon : 200 developer participants; 30 submissions/apps produced. Governance : 6 governance sessions; 10 builders in Battle of the Builders. These KPIs will be tracked on the public dashboard and reported against post-event. The 2025 Summit set a precedent by publishing full KPI results publicly HERE. 9. Will Cardano Foundation charge for tickets and accept sponsorships? Yes, tickets will be charged but at a lower per ticket price ranging from $30 (ecosystem day) and $150 to $350. Similar to last year, provision will be made for significant discount offerings ranging from 10% to 50% for community members based on chain activity, and payments in ada. Also early bird discounts will be offered at the launch of the online sale. We continue to believe that generating commercial revenue through sponsorships, ticket sales, and partnerships must remain the way forward. 10. Why should the Treasury fund the Cardano Summit at all? With Voltaire and the decentralized ecosystem, the community, DReps, and funding entities are all responsible for advancing Cardano together. 2024 marked the last Summit where funding entities sponsored the flagship event directly. For 2025 a treasury proposal was agreed as being the way to proceed for the ecosystem. Ever since 2024 we have been clear on the fact that CF can not absorb more than the usual operational overhead of the Summit, as is foreseen by this proposal. We believe that the Summit serves a strategic growth function for the Ecosystem. It provides a primary opportunity for the Cardano ecosystem to showcase Cardano to the wider audience: enterprise decision-makers, governance actors, institutional partners, regulators, and media. This is part of creating demand and increasing trust towards Cardano and its builders. The institutional relationships and press coverage generated by the Summit directly support ecosystem-wide KPIs around enterprise adoption, TVL growth, and developer onboarding. This is comparable with other Layer 1 protocols and industry practice. The sustainability of the Summit remains the goal and it is a long term target to be achieved over several years. The revenue model is building: the 2025 Summit generated USD 313K in commercial revenue, and the 2026 target is USD 450K (+50%), even in a bear market. All 2026 revenue will be set aside for 2027 expenditure, the same as in 2025. 11. Is the Cardano Foundation asking its community to fund a corporate marketing event? The Summit is not a corporate marketing event. It is the primary institutional convention for the Cardano ecosystem. The programme includes governance workshops for DReps, hackathons for developers, enterprise tech talks, regulatory roundtables, and builder showcases. Day 1 is specifically dedicated to the community (Ecosystem Day), and the event as a whole is structured to serve governance, builder, enterprise, and institutional audiences. 12. How does Cardano’s event spending compare to other L1 ecosystems? Leading L1 ecosystems invest heavily in flagship events and conference sponsorships. Solana has hosted Breakpoint alongside TOKEN2049 in the past; Sui runs SuiFest Singapore; Ethereum hosts a range of conferences. These ecosystems recognise that institutional and developer mindshare is won at premier global events. The total Treasury ask is comparable to, or below, what competing ecosystems spend on equivalent event strategies. 13. Why is the proposal being submitted outside of the Intersect budget process? The Intersect budget process projects its first treasury withdrawals to be submitted in late June, with the first funds paid out in late August or September 2026. With both events scheduled for October 2026, an August/September withdrawal timeline was simply not feasible. 14. What happens if the vote does not pass? If this proposal does not pass, the Cardano Summit 2026 will not happen. The Foundation will refocus its activities and look to other opportunities for reduced enterprise/institutional activations. 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic

items.description: Welcome to the Cardano Community Digest! Published by the Cardano Foundation Community Team every two weeks, this Digest will provide you with news, updates and events about the project and ecosystem! If you are interested in receiving the Community Digest in the future directly via email, please sign-up here ! In this edition of the Community Digest, we highlight Midnight Mainnet Launch: After six years of development, Midnight is now live, enabling privacy-preserving applications using zero-knowledge proofs. The rollout begins in phases, with ecosystem expansion and interoperability planned for later in 2026. FluidTokens Atomic Swap Breakthrough: FluidTokens completed the first native Bitcoin–Cardano atomic swap on mainnet, enabling trustless BTC–ADA trading without bridges, custodians, or wrapped assets. Cardano Node 10.7.0 Pre-Release: Intersect MBO introduced a new node version featuring major improvements, including reduced RAM usage via LedgerDB V2, alongside updates preparing for the upcoming Van Rossum hard fork. Upcoming SPO Call (April 2): IOG invites SPOs to discuss Node 10.7.0, Mithril progress, Dingo developments, and the path toward the next hard fork. Ambassador Story – Neal Lam: New Ambassador Neal Lam shares his journey into Web3 and his focus on community building, user experience, and long-term ecosystem growth. Community Learning & Dev Engagement: Recent sessions covered DeFi liquidity proposals, node diversity with Amaru, the Cardano Africa Tech Summit, and AI-powered analytics through CAP. Cardano Foundation Updates: The Foundation shared progress on its Lisbon-based accelerator cohort, new research on validator incentives, and a deep dive into market makers in crypto. Intersect Committee Elections Space (March 31): Intersect MBO hosts an X Space to explain committee roles, election details, and how members can participate. All this and more in today’s Digest. Midnight Mainnet officially Launched After more than six years of development, the Midnight Foundation announced on March 30, 2026, that the Midnight network is officially live. As per the announcement, Midnight enables applications where user data stays private while sensitive conditions can still be proven on-chain, using zero-knowledge proofs to verify information without exposing the underlying data. The launch is being rolled out in phases, with support from partners including Google Cloud, MoneyGram, and Blockdaemon. As a partner chain in the Cardano ecosystem, Midnight now enters its next stage of network and ecosystem expansion, with a rewards-enabled testnet expected in Q2 2026 and full interoperability targeted for Q3 2026. For the full announcement post, click here FluidTokens: First Atomic Swap Between Cardano and Bitcoin On March 26, 2026, FluidTokens announced the first atomic swap between Cardano and Bitcoin on mainnet. As they shared, “We just performed the first Atomic Swap between Cardano and Bitcoin in Mainnet. This means native BTC was traded for native ADA.” The swap, 50 ADA for 0.0001 BTC, was executed peer-to-peer, without bridges, custodians, or wrapped assets. Instead, it relies on cryptographic scripts on both chains. Bitcoin uses hashed timelock contracts (HTLCs) to lock funds with a secret. Once that secret is revealed, it enables the counterparty to unlock funds on Cardano. Timeouts ensure that if either party does not complete their side, funds can be safely reclaimed. While atomic swaps are not new, enabling one between Cardano and Bitcoin, two chains with very different architectures, marks a notable step forward in cross-chain interoperability. Check out the announcement post here . For a more comprehensive explanation of what this all means, look no further, as Cardano Yoda, has got you covered. You can read his full post here Cardano Node: Pre-Release Version 10.7.0 On March 26, 2026, Intersect MBO announced a pre-release of Cardano Node 10.7.0. As per the GitHub release notes, “Node version 10.7.0 contains a number of major improvements,” including a new LSM Tree storage backend (LedgerDB V2) for the UTxO-HD OnDisk backend, cutting RAM needs from 24GB to 8GB. Other updates include KES Agent support, an experimental cardano-rpc, new dmq-node and kes-agent binaries, and TLS/SSL support in cardano-tracer. The release is ready for testing - in preparation for the expected Van Rossum hard fork. But before we get to that, Intersect’s Parameter Committee is also updating the Plutus cost model - something that definitely will require developers to check their scripts against new primitives and adjusted coefficients. Read the full release notes here . Also covered in the Intersect MBO weekly update All SPOs: Join the Monthly SPO Call on April 2 All (aspiring) SPOs are invited to join the upcoming Monthly SPO Call, scheduled for Thursday, April 2 at 15:00 UTC. As per IOG’s invitation, the session will cover several updates, including Node version 10.7.0 and its newly released LSM, an update on the path toward the Van Rossem hard fork, the latest progress and near-term direction for Mithril, and developments around Dingo. For more details, and to add the event to your calendar, check out the following link: https://luma.com/zju92qz5 Ambassador Stories, with Neal Lam (Sidan Lab) Meet Neal Lam @NealSIDAN , one of the newest Ambassadors to join the Cardano Ambassador Program. Based in Hong Kong, Neal’s journey went from banking and mobile apps to UI/UX, then finally landing in blockchain and Web3. That mix gives him a unique perspective on products development, users’ wishes, and building for the long term. He was drawn to Cardano for its security, decentralization, and focus on real, lasting impact - values that match how he thinks about trust and sustainability. As an Ambassador, Neal is all about connecting people. From events and workshops to showing newcomers around Hong Kong, he helps the community feel more approachable and welcoming. He hopes to see Cardano grow steadily with more real-world adoption, stronger DeFi infrastructure, and more builders joining the ecosystem, without losing what makes it special. His message: “Cardano feels like home. Let’s keep showing up for each other and growing together as a family.” Oh, and yes… want to hear how a banking trainee ended up building in blockchain full-time? Catch his full story here. Cardanians: Weekly Ecosystem Updates In the latest Cardanians Ecosystem Newsletter, several developments across the Cardano ecosystem stand out. According to the update, Midnight’s NIGHT token was listed on Binance, becoming the first CNA on the exchange. The newsletter also mentions the upcoming release of a physical Cardano Card (remember WireX ?), a move that builds further on the existing virtual card for ada payments. And that’s not all, as it also covers a swift update on FluidTokens, which continues work on its Bitcoin–Cardano bridge, moving closer to enabling BTC liquidity on Cardano. For this and more, view here the X thread . Spotlight on Cardano Content Creators This week, we’re highlighting some of Cardano’s content creators, community members who help keep the ecosystem informed and engaged. Whether through tutorials, blogs, or thought-provoking discussions, they contribute valuable context and keep the conversation moving. Here are a few creators making an impact: Peter Bui (Learn Cardano) Peter Bui, Cardano Ambassador, SPO of ADAOZ Pool, and creator of the Learn Cardano YouTube channel, recently broke down two, highly spoken of, ecosystem updates in plain English. 1. The announcement of FluidToken’s native atomic swaps between Bitcoin and ada - with no bridge, no wrapping, no middleman. Real BTC for real ada, trustlessly enforced by cryptographic contracts on both chains! He also dives into what this all unlocks in terms of direct Bitcoin DeFi on Cardano and the removal of any kind of reliance on centralized exchanges. 2nd, the Cardano’s Van Rossem hard fork (Protocol Version 11). Thee a lot ongoing here, and Peter is clearly on top of it all. He speaks about the five new Plutus built-in functions, making every DApp faster, cheaper, with better data handling (like constant-time array lookups) and ZK-ready capabilities. I know it’s a mouth ful, but trust me, its worth a watch! These upgrades strengthen Cardano’s smart contract foundation and cross-chain interoperability. Watch It Here cexplorer.io Cexplorer.io recently dropped a super informative article on their Cardano Stablecoin Dashboard, your one-stop hub to track stablecoin action in real time. The dashboard shows net flow, market cap, dominance, and mint/burn events, plus an interactive chart breaking down transactions, volume, and holders per epoch. It tracks USDCx, USDM, USDA, DJED, iUSD, USDC via Wanchain, and USDT via Wanchain, making it easy to see supply moves, market trends, and who’s leading the stablecoin game, all in one place. Read the full article here . These creators are just a snapshot of the many creators within our ecosystem. Following them is a great way to stay updated on tutorials, interviews, and discussions that help deepen your understanding of Cardano and its potential. Community Learning & Developer Engagement Developer Office Hours Participation in the Cardano Developer Office Hours continues to grow, with developers actively tuning in to learn, share knowledge, and interact live with participants. Recent sessions featured: Governance Hour #1 - Deep Dive Into Cardano Defi Liquidity Budget - IIn this Governance Hour, Dr. Nick Schaub, also known as Elder Millennial, walks us through the Cardano DeFi Liquidity Budget proposal. The session dives into the thinking behind the proposal, with a clear goal to go beyond the written details, ask questions, and better understand its goals, structure, and potential impact on the ecosystem. More details, and the link to the recording can be found here on the Cardano Forum . Amaru & Node Diversity: Strengthening Cardano’s Infrastructure - In this Cardano Developers Office Hour, Matthias Benkort, (Dr.) Roland Kuhn, Eric Torreborre, and Julien Eluard dive into Amaru, Cardano’s new Rust-based full node, and the 2026 Budget Proposal. The session explores why client diversity is now essential for a resilient blockchain, how Amaru helps reduce systemic risk, and how the proposed budget supports a multi-node ecosystem including Haskell, Rust, and Go implementations. Missed it? Watch here . Cardano Africa Tech Summit - The Story, with Wada - In this Cardano Seminar, Megan Hess (Operations Lead at Wada Global) and Darlington Wleh (Founder of Blockchain Center Nairobi) walk us through the story behind the Cardano Africa Tech Summit. The session covers how the event came together, the key players behind the scenes, what it took to organize a summit of this scale in Africa for the first time, and much more. Watch here . Cardano Analytics Platform (CAP), powered by LLM - In this Cardano Seminar, Marcio Moreno and Rafael Brandao, co-founders of MOBR Systems, introduce the Cardano Analytics Platform (CAP) and how AI is transforming access to on-chain data. The session explores how CAP’s semantic analytics layer, natural language queries, smart dashboards, and knowledge-graph technology make on-chain insights more accessible for research, governance, and other use cases across the Cardano ecosystem. Watch here . These sessions are just a few examples of the many ongoing ecosystem engagement efforts across Cardano. To stay updated and not miss upcoming episodes, be sure to give them a follow, or subscribe to their channel. Updates from the Cardano Foundation The Cardano Foundation has shared several recent updates, highlighting innovation, ecosystem growth, and research. One highlight is the Cardano Accelerator Program Spring ’26 Cohort in Lisbon. The Foundation’s Venture Hub is supporting five DeFi and RWA ventures — Colossus Digital, Libertum, NOBON, The Mint, and Toto Finance — through a 10-week program combining technical guidance, business coaching, workshops, and fundraising support. The cohort will conclude with a Demo Day for investors and ecosystem partners. Learn more here: Cardano Accelerator Program In the latest episode of Let’s Talk Cardano , Jonathan Mathai, Director at G20 Strategies, explores the role of market makers in crypto, DeFi, and traditional finance. The discussion covers liquidity creation in order book and AMM markets, risk management, yield generation, and how market makers navigate volatility, MEV, and AI. Ever wanted to learn about MEV or AMM markets, well, this one’s for you! Watch or listen here: YouTube | Spotify The Foundation also published new research on validator incentives and restaking security, in collaboration with IOG and Gauntlet. The study identifies structural vulnerabilities in current restaking designs, showing that no slashing mechanism can simultaneously satisfy several desirable properties while removing Sybil attack incentives. As Cardano’s reserve emissions decline over time, understanding sustainable validator rewards becomes increasingly important. The research was presented at the 5th Workshop on Decentralized Finance (DeFi) in March 2026, providing a foundation for exploring alternative mechanisms that support long-term network security.
